definition_zh: 与……有关联；与……有联系；伴随出现；与……共事交往；与……结盟联合；是……的风险因素；使人联想到；与……有牵连；与……相对应
definition_en: to be connected with something or someone, whether by a statistical link, a shared setting, a personal or institutional tie, a risk factor, a memory, a suspicion or a conceptual correspondence
core_image: 一张统计图上两条曲线同向起落，旁边用一条细线把它们连到同一个坐标点，却没有标出箭头方向
scene: 保险公司把十年的理赔记录摊在桌上，两条曲线在图上同向起落，分析员用红笔把它们连到同一个点。 Smoking can be associated with a higher risk of lung disease in long-term studies.
sceneCN: 保险公司的桌上摊着成叠的理赔单（第 1 个义项：统计相关）；句意为在长期研究中，吸烟可能与更高的肺病风险相关。图中可辨识物件：理赔记录、两条同向起伏的曲线、坐标纸、红笔。

pos.zh: 与……有关联；与……有联系；伴随出现；与……有牵连

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁动词「associare」经分词形式而来，义为「使关联；结交；同事」
加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「协会；联想；关联」
加形容词尾构成，义为「联想的；结合的」
同出「socius」，义为「社会的；社交的」

senses.title: Statistical correlation
senses.definition: to show a measurable statistical link with another variable, without showing that one causes the other
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个变量之间存在可测量的统计联系，且不表示一方导致另一方
senses.example: Higher income can be associated with longer life expectancy in national surveys.
senses.exampleCN: 在各国调查中，较高的收入可能与更长的预期寿命相关。
senses.why: The passive frame came from the idea of joining two things, and statistics uses it for two quantities that rise and fall together.
senses.whyCN: 被动框架来自「把两样东西连在一起」的观念，统计学用它指两个同时起落的量。

senses.title: Co-occurrence
senses.definition: to appear at the same time or in the same setting as something else, without a claim about cause
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物在同一时间或同一场合出现，不带因果断言
senses.example: Swallows can be associated with the arrival of warm spring weather.
senses.exampleCN: 燕子可能与温暖春天气息的到来同时出现。
senses.why: If two things are seen together often enough, the mind joins them before any proof of cause exists.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西若常被一起看到，人会在有因果证据之前先把它们连起来。

senses.title: Working or mixing with people
senses.definition: to spend time, work or cooperate with a person, especially in a professional or social setting
senses.definitionCN: 与某人在职业或社交场合相处、共事或合作
senses.example: Junior researchers may be associated with senior scholars on a long project.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻研究者可能在长期项目中与资深学者共事。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the Latin word is companionship, so the phrase still covers people who keep company.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最古老的意思是伙伴关系，因此该短语仍指与人交往共事。

senses.title: Alliance with an organisation
senses.definition: to be formally linked to an institution as a member, partner or ally
senses.definitionCN: 作为成员、伙伴或盟友与某个机构建立正式联系
senses.example: The new clinic can be associated with a teaching hospital in the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家新诊所能与同城的一家教学医院建立联合关系。
senses.why: Institutions join the way people do, and the same passive phrase marks the partnership.
senses.whyCN: 机构之间的联合与人之间的结交同构，同一个被动短语标出这种伙伴关系。

senses.title: A risk factor for disease
senses.definition: to be statistically linked to a disease as a factor that raises its likelihood
senses.definitionCN: 作为提高患病可能性的因素，与某种疾病存在统计联系
senses.example: Poor sleep can be associated with heart disease in middle age.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足可能与中年时期的心脏病相关。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the statistical frame and turned a measured link into a warning about risk.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了统计框架，把测得的联系变成了关于风险的提醒。

senses.title: Bringing a memory to mind
senses.definition: to call up a remembered person, place or feeling through resemblance or past pairing
senses.definitionCN: 通过相似或过去的配对，唤起记忆中的人、地点或感受
senses.example: For many listeners, that tune can be associated with childhood summers.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多听众来说，那段旋律可能让人联想到童年的夏天。
senses.why: The mind stores things in pairs, so one item becomes the cue that summons the other.
senses.whyCN: 心智把事物成对存放，于是一个事物成为唤起另一个的线索。

senses.title: Implication in a scandal
senses.definition: to be connected to wrongdoing or a scandal, usually with damage to reputation
senses.definitionCN: 与不当行为或丑闻扯上关系，通常伴随名誉受损
senses.example: Two officials may be associated with the contract scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 两名官员可能与这起合同丑闻有牵连。
senses.why: A name placed next to a scandal is enough to stain it, even before any charge is proved.
senses.whyCN: 名字只要与丑闻并排出现就足以染上污点，哪怕指控尚未证实。

senses.title: Conceptual correspondence
senses.definition: to correspond to another item within a model, mapping or system of symbols
senses.definitionCN: 在模型、映射或符号系统中与另一项相对应
senses.example: In this model, each symbol can be associated with one physical quantity.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个模型中，每个符号可以与一个物理量相对应。
senses.why: A model is a set of paired entries, and the phrase names the link between the two columns.
senses.whyCN: 模型就是一组成对的条目，该短语指两列之间的对应关系。

intro.en: Associate comes from Latin associare, to join together, built from ad-, toward, and socius, a companion or ally. The same socius underlies social, society and sociable, and English later fixed the passive frame be associated with for every kind of link.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语的「associare」「联合」，由「ad-」「朝向」与「socius」「同伴、盟友」构成。同一个「socius」也是「social」「society」「sociable」的来源；英语后来固定了被动框架「be associated with」，用来表示各种联系。

items.en: Socius meant a companion, ally or partner, someone who shares something with another person.
items.cn: 「socius」指同伴、盟友或伙伴，即与他人共享某物的人。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant toward, and before a word it marked direction or attachment.
items.cn: 前缀「ad-」意为朝向，加在词前表示方向或附着。

items.en: Joining ad- to socius produced associare, to unite with or keep company with another.
items.cn: 把「ad-」与「socius」合起来得到「associare」，意为与……联合或与……为伴。

items.en: Its past participle associatus meant joined or united, and it supplied the shape of the English adjective.
items.cn: 其过去分词「associatus」意为已联合的，为英语的形容词形式提供了形状。

items.en: English adopted associate as a verb for joining with another, and as a noun for a colleague or partner.
items.cn: 英语把「associate」用作动词表示与人结交，也用作名词表示同事或伙伴。

items.en: The passive phrase be associated with later became the standard wording for statistical, medical and social links.
items.cn: 被动短语「be associated with」后来成为统计、医学与社会联系的通用说法。

note.en: The first group looks and sounds like associate; the second group contrasts three ways of linking things: associated with reports a link that may be statistical, social or accidental, characterized by names the defining mark of a thing, and composed of names the parts that make a whole.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「associate」相近；第二组对照三种连接方式：「associated with」表示可能是统计、社交或偶然的联系，「characterized by」指出事物的定义性标志，「composed of」指出构成整体的各个部分。

entries.definition: To join with another as a colleague, partner or companion, or such a colleague.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为同事、伙伴或同伴与人结交，也指这样的同事。

entries.definition: The noun for a society, a partnership or a mental link between ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 指协会、伙伴关系，或观念之间的心理联系。

entries.definition: Relating to mental connection between one idea and another.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个观念与另一个观念之间的心理联系。

entries.definition: To separate one thing from another in the mind or in law, the opposite direction of association.
entries.definitionCN: 指在心里或法律上把一事物与另一事物分开，是关联的反方向。

entries.definition: Concerning people living together; it comes from socius but no longer carries a link in the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们共同生活的；同出「socius」，但在短语中已不表示具体联系。

entries.definition: To be connected with something, often without the statistical or personal shades of associated with.
entries.definitionCN: 指与某事物相连，通常不带「associated with」的统计或人际色彩。

entries.definition: To vary together in a measured way; narrower than associated with, because it demands a statistical measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指以可测量的方式共同变化；比「associated with」窄，因为它要求统计度量。

entries.definition: To have a defining mark that identifies the thing; it states a feature, not a statistical link.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有可识别事物的定义性标志；它陈述特征，而非统计联系。

entries.definition: To consist of parts that make up a whole; it answers what the thing is made of, not what it is linked to.
entries.definitionCN: 指由构成整体的各个部分组成；它回答事物由什么做成，而非与什么相连。

entries.definition: To be officially attached to an organisation, a narrower institutional version of associated with.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式隶属于某机构，是「associated with」较窄的机构版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real family of socius and the everyday settings where the phrase appears.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「socius」的真实同族词，以及该短语出现的日常场景。

normal.en: Socius is the Latin companion behind social, society and sociable.
normal.cn: 「socius」是拉丁语里的同伴，也是「social」「society」「sociable」的来源。

normal.en: A shared office, a shared project and a shared surname all make two things associated.
normal.cn: 共用的办公室、共同的项目、共同的姓氏，都会让两样东西产生关联。

normal.en: Statistics says associated, never causes, when two curves only move together.
normal.cn: 两条曲线只是同向移动时，统计学只说「associated」，从不说「causes」。

normal.en: Doctors say a habit can be associated with a disease when the link holds across many studies.
normal.cn: 当联系在多份研究中都成立时，医生会说某种习惯可能与某种疾病相关。

normal.en: In memory, one smell can be associated with a whole kitchen from childhood.
normal.cn: 在记忆里，一种气味可能让人联想到童年整间厨房。

abstract.en: Association is a line drawn between two things before anyone knows which way cause runs.
abstract.cn: 关联是在还没人知道因果方向时，先在两样东西之间画的一条线。

abstract.en: The same phrase serves a colleague, a hospital and a risk factor, because all three are names joined to another name.
abstract.cn: 同一个短语可指同事、医院与风险因素，因为这三者都是与另一个名字并排的名字。

abstract.en: A scandal spreads by adjacency: one name beside another is already a stain.
abstract.cn: 丑闻靠相邻关系扩散：一个名字挨着另一个名字，就已经是污点。

examples.en: The survey shows that long commutes can be associated with stress.
examples.cn: 这项调查显示，长时间通勤可能与压力相关。

examples.en: Her early papers can be associated with a research group in Kyoto.
examples.cn: 她早期的论文可能与京都的一个研究小组有关联。

examples.en: In the story, the broken watch can be associated with his lost brother.
examples.cn: 在故事里，那只坏掉的手表可能让人联想到他失踪的弟弟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 呃搜西埃提德 威兹」——把两样东西并排写在同一行，中间画一道细线：有关联、有来往

root: 拉丁语「associare」「联合」由「ad-」「朝向」与「socius」「同伴、盟友」构成；同族词有「social」「society」「sociable」。英语用被动框架「be associated with」把统计相关、伴随出现、人际交往、机构结盟、疾病风险、记忆联想、丑闻牵连与概念对应都收进同一个短语。注意它只说明「有联系」，既不说明因果，也不说明构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one frame: the link may be measured, observed, social, institutional, medical, remembered, suspected or conceptual.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个框架：这种联系可以是测量出来的、观察到的、人际的、机构的、医学的、记忆的、被怀疑的或概念上的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two names are written side by side and a thin line joins them, with no arrow of cause.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个名字并排写着，一条细线把它们连起来，却没有表示因果的箭头。

branches.en: THE MEASURED LINK: two quantities move together, and medicine reads the same frame as risk.
branches.cn: 测量的联系：两个量一起变动，医学把同一框架读作风险。

branches.en: THE SHARED SETTING: two things appear in the same place or time, with no cause claimed.
branches.cn: 共同场合：两样东西在同一地点或时间出现，不断言因果。

branches.en: THE JOINED PARTY: a person keeps company with another, or an institution joins an ally.
branches.cn: 联合的一方：一个人与另一个人交往，或一个机构与盟友结盟。

branches.en: THE MEMORY CUE: one thing summons another that was stored beside it.
branches.cn: 记忆线索：一个事物唤起曾与它一起存放的另一个。

branches.en: THE SUSPECTED OR MAPPED LINK: a name beside a scandal, or a symbol matched to a quantity.
branches.cn: 被怀疑或映射的联系：名字挨着丑闻，或符号对应某个量。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin verb whose core is socius, a companion, and the family still runs through English social vocabulary.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个拉丁动词构成，其核心是「socius」「同伴」，这一族词仍贯穿英语的社会类词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies socius, the prefix ad- and the verb associare; English adds the passive frame and the noun and adjective endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「socius」、前缀「ad-」与动词「associare」；英语加上了被动框架以及名词与形容词词尾。

items.example: Socius named a person who shares something with another.
items.exampleCN: 「socius」指与他人共享某物的人。

items.example: The prefix points the action toward another party.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向另一方。

items.structure: Latin verb from ad- and socius
items.example: The verb joins two parties in one act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把两方连在一个动作里。

items.example: The participle describes the state of being joined.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词描述已联合的状态。

items.meaning: to link or join; a colleague
items.example: English uses it for linking ideas and for a work partner.
items.exampleCN: 英语用它表示连接观念，也指工作伙伴。

items.meaning: a society or a mental link
items.example: The noun names both an organisation and a mental connection.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指组织，也指心理联系。

items.example: The adjective describes thinking that works by connection.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述靠联系运作的思维。

items.example: The adjective describes life with other people.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述与他人共同的生活。

items.example: The noun names a community held together by shared rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指由共同规则维系的人群。

items.example: The adjective describes a person who enjoys the company of others.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指喜欢与他人相处的人。

definition_zh: 语言；言语；（某一领域的）表达方式；计算机语言
definition_en: a system of spoken or written signs used for communication, or a particular style or code of expression
core_image: 一张围着许多人的旧木桌，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页，几个人正用手势和声音相互回应
scene: 旧木桌旁围坐着来自几座村镇的人，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页。 Language was the only tool they had in common that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里指「用于交流的声音与符号系统」（第 1 个义项：人类交流的整体系统）；句意为那天下午，语言是他们唯一共同拥有的工具。可辨识物件：旧木桌、纸页、不同文字、手势。

pos.zh: 语言；言语；表达方式（可数与不可数两用）

senses.title: The human system of communication
senses.titleCN: 人类用于交流的符号系统
senses.definition: the shared system of sounds, words and grammar by which people communicate
senses.definitionCN: 人们借以交流的声音、词汇与语法的共享系统
senses.example: Language is learned in company, not from a dictionary alone.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是在与人相处中学到的，而不是只靠词典。
senses.why: the word came from the Latin name for the tongue, so the oldest image is the organ that produces speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语对「舌头」的称呼，因此最古老的画面是发出言语的器官。

senses.title: A particular named tongue
senses.definition: a specific system such as Chinese, Arabic or Swahili, counted as one item
senses.definitionCN: 如汉语、阿拉伯语或斯瓦希里语等具体系统，可作为一个单位计数
senses.example: She speaks four languages and reads two more.
senses.exampleCN: 她会说四种语言，还能读另外两种。
senses.why: once the general capacity was recognized, each separate system needed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 当整体能力被认出之后，每一个独立的系统也需要同一个名称。

senses.title: Speech as it is actually used
senses.definition: the spoken words of a person or group on a given occasion, as opposed to writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体在某一场合说出的具体话语，与书面语相对
senses.example: His language in the meeting was far plainer than his letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上说的话比他的书信朴素得多。
senses.why: the tongue is the instrument of speech, so the word also names the spoken output itself.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是说话的器官，因此这个词也指说出来的产物。

senses.title: The style and wording of a text
senses.definition: the choice of words and sentence patterns that gives a text its tone
senses.definitionCN: 使文本形成某种语气的用词与句式选择
senses.example: The language of the report was careful but cold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的措辞谨慎而冷淡。
senses.why: a text's manner of speech can be described with the same word used for a nation's tongue.
senses.whyCN: 一个文本的说话方式，可以用描述民族语言的同一个词来指称。

senses.title: The vocabulary of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业的行话与术语
senses.definition: the technical words and conventions used by a profession or subject
senses.definitionCN: 某职业或学科使用的术语与惯例
senses.example: Legal language keeps ordinary readers at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 法律行话把普通读者挡在门外。
senses.why: a profession speaks its own tongue, so its terms are called a language.
senses.whyCN: 一个职业说自己的话，因此其术语被称作一种语言。

senses.title: A code for machines
senses.definition: a formal set of instructions that a computer can process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机可以处理的一套形式化指令
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课一次只教一种编程语言。
senses.why: the word was extended to any rule-governed code, including one no human speaks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被扩展到任何有规则的代码，包括没有人说的那种。

senses.title: Non-verbal signals
senses.definition: meaning carried by gesture, posture or tone rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由手势、姿态或语气而非词语承载的意义
senses.example: Her body language said more than her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肢体语言比回答说明了更多。
senses.why: meaning is carried without the tongue at all, and the word follows the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意义完全不经舌头而传递，词也跟着意义走。

senses.title: The human capacity for speech
senses.titleCN: 人类拥有语言的天赋能力
senses.definition: the general human ability to acquire and use a grammar, studied as a faculty
senses.definitionCN: 人类习得并使用语法的总体能力，被当作一种官能来研究
senses.example: Language separates human communication from simple signalling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言使人类交流区别于简单的信号传递。
senses.why: the most abstract sense returns to the original faculty that makes every other sense possible.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的义项回到那项使其他所有义项成为可能的原初官能。

intro.en: Language comes from Old French langage, from Latin lingua 'tongue, language'. The further origin of lingua is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 langage，再上溯拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」。lingua 更早的来源未获证明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant both 'tongue' and 'language'. The sense grew from the organ to what the organ produces, a common pattern in many languages.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」。词义从器官转到器官的产物，这在许多语言中都是常见模式。

items.en: The deeper origin of lingua is unsettled. A link sometimes proposed with a verb meaning 'to lick' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lingua 更深的来源没有定论。有人提出它与一个表「舔」的动词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French langage named speech and the way one speaks; English borrowed it in the age of Norman rule.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语及说话方式；英语在诺曼统治时期借入。

items.en: Middle English used the word for a nation's tongue and for a person's manner of speech, both senses surviving today.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指一个民族的语言，也指个人的说话方式，两义都留存至今。

items.en: Modern technical life extended the word to formal codes, giving programming languages, and to gesture, giving body language.
items.cn: 现代技术生活把词扩展到形式化代码，产生「编程语言」，也扩展到姿态，产生「肢体语言」。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested pre-Latin form of lingua is agreed, and the exact route through French is reconstructed from later records.
items.cn: 来源不确定：lingua 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认书证，经法语传入的确切路径亦由较晚记录构拟。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same root that are often confused; group two holds near neighbours that name communication.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词；第二组是表示交流的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it never names the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，本身不指那套系统。

entries.definition: The scientific study of language, not a language and not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对语言的科学研究，既不是一种语言，也不是一个人。

entries.definition: A person who studies language, or loosely one who knows several.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，或宽泛地指通晓多种语言的人。

entries.definition: An informal word for a foreign language or a jargon; it is playful where language is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指外语或行话的口语说法，语气戏谑，而「语言」一词为中性。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of speaking; it covers sound but not writing or the abstract system.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话的行为或场合，覆盖声音，却不含书面语或抽象系统。

entries.definition: An old word for a language, as in the mother tongue; it is close but archaic in most uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指语言的旧说法，如「母语」；意思接近，但多数用法已古旧。

entries.definition: One variety within a language; calling it a language is a political judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种语言内部的变体；称它为「语言」常是政治判断。

entries.definition: Any system of signs with rules, including machines; it lacks the human and social weight of language.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何有规则的符号系统，包括机器；缺少语言的人类与社会分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'tongue', so the word begins as the body part that makes speech.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词最初就是制造言语的身体部位。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: foreign language, body language, programming language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：外语、肢体语言、编程语言。

normal.en: The adjective, the discipline and the person all come from the same root.
normal.cn: 形容词、学科与人都出自同一词根。

normal.en: The family runs linguistic, linguistics, linguist, multilingual, bilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言的」「语言学」「语言学家」「多语的」「双语的」。

normal.en: Counting languages uses the plural, speaking in general uses the singular.
normal.cn: 数具体语言用复数，泛指说话能力用单数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every sheet is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每张纸都出自不同的笔迹。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built from sounds rather than stones.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用声音而非石头搭成的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens a different door for every listener.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙，对每个听者打开不同的一扇门。

examples.en: Language changes faster in cities than in isolated valleys.
examples.cn: 语言在城市里的变化比在封闭山谷中更快。

examples.en: The two communities share a border but not a language.
examples.cn: 这两个社群共享一条边界，却不共享一种语言。

examples.en: Nurses are trained to read the body language of anxious patients.
examples.cn: 护士受过训练，能读懂焦虑病人的肢体语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兰格维吉」——拦住陌生人开口，靠的就是这套声音与符号的系统。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 进入英语；词义由器官转向器官的产物。lingua 更深来源不确定，与表「舔」动词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one organ: the tongue produces speech, speech becomes a named system, that system takes styles and jargons, and the same word is finally lent to machines and to silent gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个器官铺开：舌头产生言语，言语成为具名的系统，系统又生出风格与行话，最后同一个词被借给机器与无声的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table, many scripts, and hands answering in gesture and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子、多种文字，人们用手势与声音相互回应。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: the human faculty and its shared system are the two sides of one coin.
branches.cn: 能力：人类的官能与共享系统是同一枚硬币的两面。

branches.en: COUNTED TONGUES: each separate system can be named and counted.
branches.cn: 可数的语言：每一套独立系统都可被命名与计数。

branches.en: BEYOND WORDS: actual speech and silent gesture both carry meaning.
branches.cn: 超出词语：实际说出的话与无声的姿态都承载意义。

branches.en: TONE OF A TEXT: word choice alone can make writing warm or cold.
branches.cn: 文本的语气：仅靠选词就能让文字变暖或变冷。

branches.en: RULED CODES: a profession's jargon and a machine's instructions are both governed sets.
branches.cn: 有规则的代码：专业行话与机器指令都是受规则支配的集合。

intro.en: The word is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin root meaning 'tongue', and that root also builds the whole linguistic family.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语成形的名词，建在拉丁语表「舌头」的词根上，这个词根也构成整个「语言」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, linguist and linguistics through French and Latin endings; the same root appears in the adjective for 'tongue-shaped'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 经法语与拉丁词尾衍生出「语言」「语言学家」与「语言学」；同一词根也出现在表「舌形」的形容词里。

items.meaning: the organ of speech, and speech itself
items.example: The root already carries both the body part and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根已同时带着器官与其产物。

items.example: Language is older than any dictionary.
items.exampleCN: 语言比任何词典都古老。

items.example: The linguist recorded the last speakers.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家记录了最后的说话者。

items.example: Linguistic evidence dated the text.
items.exampleCN: 语言证据为这份文本定了年代。

items.example: Linguistics became a university subject.
items.exampleCN: 语言学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: Bilingual signs appeared at the airport.
items.exampleCN: 机场出现了双语标识。

items.example: The city is proudly multilingual.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市以多语并存为荣。

items.example: The manual is full of technical lingo.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册满是技术行话。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 双舌的；使用两种语言的

definition_zh: 偏爱；优先；优待；优先权
definition_en: the choosing of one thing over another, or the right to be served or paid before others
core_image: 一只盘子里的两块点心本一模一样，拿筷子的人却每次都先夹靠左那一块，动作快得像是早已决定
scene: 早上七点，车站售票窗口前拉起了两列队伍，戴徽章的工作人员把一侧的人先引到柜台前。 Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
sceneCN: 这里本词指优先安排或优先照顾（第 2 个义项：把先办、先得的次序给别人）；句意为座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 偏爱；更喜欢的事物（可数或不可数）
优先；优先权（不可数）
（贸易或关税上的）优惠待遇

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀，回到同族动词，语义偏移为「更喜欢；宁愿」
由本词加表关系的形容词后缀构成，语义偏移为「优先的；优待的」
由同族形容词加表方式的副词后缀构成，语义偏移为「最好是」
由同族动词加表「可……的」后缀构成，语义偏移为「更可取的」
由本词加表股份的名词构成，语义偏移为「优先股」

senses.title: Liking one thing more
senses.definition: a stronger liking for one thing than for another
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的喜欢超过对另一物的喜欢
senses.example: Her preference is for strong tea rather than coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 她偏爱浓茶而非咖啡。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to carry a thing in front; what is put in front is what one favours.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为把某物搬到前面；被放到前面，就是被偏爱的。

senses.title: The right to be served first
senses.definition: the right or practice of being dealt with before others
senses.definitionCN: 先于他人得到办理或照顾的权利或做法
senses.example: Give your preference to families with small children when seats are limited.
senses.exampleCN: 座位有限时优先安排带幼儿的家庭。
senses.why: Being placed before others is a literal carrying forward, so the noun marks rank as well as taste.
senses.whyCN: 被放在他人之前，正是字面意义上的搬到前面，因此该名词也标出次序。

senses.title: A trade advantage
senses.definition: a lower tariff or easier terms granted to certain trading partners
senses.definitionCN: 给予某些贸易伙伴的较低关税或更宽条件
senses.example: The agreement grants tariff preference to the smallest exporters.
senses.exampleCN: 该协议给予最小规模的出口商关税优惠。
senses.why: A partner carried to the front of the queue is a partner who pays less at the border.
senses.whyCN: 被提到队伍前面的伙伴，就是在关境上付款更少的伙伴。

senses.title: A first claim in law
senses.definition: the right of one creditor to be paid before others from a debtor's property
senses.definitionCN: 某一债权人从债务人财产中先于他人受偿的权利
senses.example: The bank's preference over the land was recorded at the registry.
senses.exampleCN: 银行对这块地的优先受偿权已在登记处记录。
senses.why: Law keeps the order of payment literal: one claim is carried ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 法律把付款次序说得很字面：一项债权被搬到其余债权之前。

senses.title: One's first choice
senses.definition: the person or thing one would choose first if only one could be had
senses.definitionCN: 若只能得到一个，会最先选择的人或物
senses.example: This route is our preference for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路线是我们过河的首选。
senses.why: Choosing is ranking, and the top of the ranking is what stands in front.
senses.whyCN: 选择就是排序，排在最前面的那一个就是被放到前面的。

senses.title: Settings stored by software
senses.definition: stored choices that tell a program how its user wants it to behave
senses.definitionCN: 程序记录下来的、说明用户希望它如何运作的选择
senses.example: The app keeps your preference even after you sign out.
senses.exampleCN: 即使退出登录，这款应用仍保留你的偏好设置。
senses.why: A machine that remembers a choice keeps a small record of what its user put first.
senses.whyCN: 会记住选择机器，就是留下用户「把什么放在前面」的小记录。

senses.title: A pattern in buying
senses.definition: the tendency of buyers to favour certain goods, brands or features
senses.definitionCN: 购买者更偏爱某些商品、品牌或特性的趋势
senses.example: Surveys track preference for local produce.
senses.exampleCN: 调查追踪消费者对本地农产品的偏好。
senses.why: Economists widen one person's taste into a measurable pattern of favouring.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把一个人的口味扩展成可测量的偏爱模式。

senses.title: A taste shaped by culture
senses.definition: a leaning in style, art or custom that a group learns rather than inherits
senses.definitionCN: 群体习得而非天生继承的风格、艺术或习俗上的偏向
senses.example: Colour preference varies sharply between regions.
senses.exampleCN: 颜色偏好在不同地区差别很大。
senses.why: Shared leaning is still a carrying forward of one option, only now by a whole group.
senses.whyCN: 共享的偏向仍然是「把某一选项搬到前面」，只是搬运者换成了一个群体。

intro.en: Preference comes from Latin praeferre 'to carry in front, place before', built from prae- 'before' and ferre 'to carry'; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语 praeferre「搬到前面、置于前面」，由表「在前」的前缀加 ferre「携带」构成；英语经法语借入。

items.en: Ferre meant 'to carry, bear, bring', one of the most common verbs of movement in Latin.
items.cn: ferre 意为「携带、承载、带来」，是拉丁语中最常见的移动动词之一。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front', whether of place or of rank.
items.cn: 表「在前」的前缀意为在位置上或次序上靠前。

items.en: Praeferre joined the two: to carry something in front of something else, hence to set one above another.
items.cn: 两相结合构成的动词意为把某物搬到另一物之前，因此引申为把某物排到另一物之上。

items.en: French made a noun of the verb, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century for the act of favouring.
items.cn: 法语把该动词名词化，英语在十四世纪借入，指偏爱的行为。

items.en: Courts and merchants narrowed the noun to a right of first payment and a lower tariff.
items.cn: 法庭与商人把该名词收窄为先受偿的权利与更低的关税。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is placed in the fourteenth century, and the older base behind ferre is generally considered a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语最早书证定于十四世纪，而 ferre 背后的更早词基一般认为是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close and are often confused with this noun; group two holds words for choosing and for liking.
note.cn: 第一组是与本词形近或音近、常被混淆的词；第二组是表示选择与喜爱的词。

entries.definition: The base verb meaning to like one thing better; the noun adds the result of that liking.
entries.definitionCN: 基干动词，意为更喜欢某物；名词则加出这种喜爱的结果。

entries.definition: The adjective built on this noun, describing treatment that gives someone first place.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词构成的形容词，描述给予某人优先地位的处理方式。

entries.definition: A noun for advancement in office, from the same verb but with a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该动词，但指职位上的升迁，义项不同。

entries.definition: An adjective saying one option is better; it evaluates rather than records a taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，表示某个选项更好；它作评价，而不记录口味。

entries.definition: The act of picking or the set of options; preference is the leaning that guides the pick.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的动作或可选范围；本词是引导挑选的那种偏向。

entries.definition: Simple fondness for something, without the sense of ranking one above another.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的朴素喜爱，不含把某物排在另一物之上的意味。

entries.definition: The state of coming first because of urgency or importance, a matter of order rather than taste.
entries.definitionCN: 因紧急或重要而排在最前，讲的是次序而非口味。

entries.definition: A favourable condition or benefit; the trade sense of preference is one kind of advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 有利条件或好处；本词的贸易义是其中一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real parts: a prefix meaning before, and a verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: 两个真实成分：一个表「在前」的前缀，加一个表「携带」的动词。

normal.en: The family runs prefer, preference, preferable, preferably, preferential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括更喜欢、偏爱、更可取的、最好是、优先的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: have a preference for, give preference to, in preference to.
normal.cn: 固定说法：偏爱、优先考虑、优先于。

normal.en: Every technical use puts somebody at the front: a creditor, an exporter, a passenger, a setting.
normal.cn: 每个专业用法都把某一方放到前面：债权人、出口商、乘客、某项设置。

normal.en: The noun records a ranking; the verb records the act of ranking.
normal.cn: 名词记录的是排序结果，动词记录的是排序的动作。

abstract.en: Picture two identical cakes on a plate and a hand that always reaches left first.
abstract.cn: 想象盘里两块一模一样的点心，一只手每次都先伸向左边。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid across a queue to mark who is let through first.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子横在队伍中，标出谁先被放行。

abstract.en: Picture a screen that remembers which button you press every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕记住了你每天早上按的那个按钮。

examples.en: He has a strong preference for quiet rooms.
examples.cn: 他非常偏爱安静的房间。

examples.en: Preference was given to applicants from the region.
examples.cn: 优先考虑了来自本地区的申请人。

examples.en: You can change your preference at any time.
examples.cn: 你随时可以更改自己的偏好设置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把「在前」与「携带」合起来看：把某样东西搬到前面，就是偏爱它、优先待它。

root: 拉丁 praeferre「搬到前面、置于前面」＝表「在前」的前缀＋ferre「携带」；英语经法语借入，由「置于前」引申为偏爱与优先；更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: an object carried to the front is the one liked, served first, taxed less, paid first, chosen first, remembered by a machine, favoured by buyers and shaped by a culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：被搬到前面的东西，就是被偏爱的、先被服务的、少缴税的、先受偿的、首选中的、被机器记住的、被买家青睐的、被文化塑造的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical cakes on a plate, and a hand that always reaches for the left one first.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘里两块一模一样的点心，一只手每次都先伸向左边的。

branches.en: TASTE AND CULTURE: one person's liking and a region's shared style are the same favouring at two scales.
branches.cn: 口味与文化：一个人的喜爱与一个地区共享的风格，是同一种偏爱在两个尺度上。

branches.en: RANK AND TRADE: being served before others and paying less at the border both mean being moved ahead.
branches.cn: 次序与贸易：先被服务与在关境少缴税，都意味着被移到前面。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLAIM: a creditor carried ahead of the rest keeps the image in strict order.
branches.cn: 法律的求偿：被搬到其余人之前的债权人，把这意象保持在严格次序里。

branches.en: THE FIRST CHOICE: what one would pick first stands at the head of a ranking.
branches.cn: 首选：最先会挑的那个，排在名单的最前。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MARKET: a stored setting and a buyer's pattern both record what is put first.
branches.cn: 机器与市场：存下的设置与买家的模式，都记录「什么被放在前面」。

intro.en: Preference is a Latin noun formed from a prefix, a carrying verb and a noun suffix; the same pieces build a small English family, so the word can be read in parts.
intro.cn: 本词是由表方向的前缀、表「携带」的动词与名词后缀构成的拉丁名词；同样的部件构成一个小英语词族，可按部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- supplies 'before' and ferre supplies 'carry'; the noun suffix names the act, and English adds nothing further.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「在前」的前缀提供「之前」之义，表「携带」的动词提供搬运义，名词后缀命名这一行为；英语不再加缀。

items.example: The verb is the carrying itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词就是「搬」这个动作本身。

items.meaning: to carry in front, to set above
items.example: To carry a thing in front is to give it the first place.
items.exampleCN: 把东西搬到前面，就是给它第一位。

items.example: The state noun named the favouring.
items.exampleCN: 这个状态名词命名偏爱。

definition_zh: 捕食者；掠食者；掠夺者
definition_en: an organism that hunts and kills others for food, or a person, firm or state that exploits weaker parties
core_image: 一头狮子伏在草坡后，目光锁定饮水处的羚羊群
scene: 这里指「捕食者」。 The lion is the only apex predator left in this valley.
sceneCN: 这里 predator 指「捕食者」（第 1 个义项：捕杀其他动物为食的生物）；狮子是这片谷地仅存的顶级捕食者。图中可辨识物件：狮子、草坡、羚羊群、水坑。

pos.zh: 捕食者；掠食者；掠夺者（可数，指动物或个人、机构）

collocations.zh: 顶级捕食者；食物链顶端物种
捕食者控制；为保护其他物种而猎杀捕食者

senses.title: An animal that hunts
senses.titleCN: 捕食动物：以捕杀为生的生物
senses.definition: an animal that captures and kills other animals for food
senses.definitionCN: 指通过捕获并杀死其他动物来获得食物的动物
senses.example: Wolves are social predators that hunt in coordinated packs.
senses.exampleCN: 狼是群居捕食者，以协同的群体方式狩猎。
senses.why: The core sense names a role in the food web, defined by behaviour rather than by species or diet alone.
senses.whyCN: 核心义项命名食物网中的一种角色，由行为而非仅仅由物种或食性界定。

senses.title: Apex predator
senses.titleCN: 顶级捕食者：成年个体几乎没有天敌
senses.definition: a predator at the top of its food chain, with no regular natural predator of its own
senses.definitionCN: 指处于食物链顶端、自身没有常规天敌的捕食者
senses.example: Removing the apex predator allowed deer to overgraze the forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 移除顶级捕食者后，鹿群把林下植被啃食过度。
senses.why: The term marks a position rather than a behaviour: the top predator regulates everything below it.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法标出的是位置而非行为：顶级捕食者调节其下所有层级。

senses.title: A person who exploits
senses.titleCN: 掠夺者：以弱者为目标的个人
senses.definition: a person who systematically exploits vulnerable people for money, power or sexual gratification
senses.definitionCN: 指为金钱、权力或性满足而系统性剥削弱势者的个人
senses.example: The court described the recruiter as a predator who targeted teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭把那名招募者描述为专门针对青少年的掠夺者。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the hunt: the vulnerable are stalked, isolated and consumed, and the harm is one-sided.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了捕猎：弱势者被跟踪、被孤立、被吞食，伤害是单向的。

senses.title: Corporate predator
senses.titleCN: 企业掠食者：以收购吞并对手的公司
senses.definition: a company that grows by aggressively buying or dismantling weaker firms
senses.definitionCN: 指通过激进收购或拆解较弱企业而壮大的公司
senses.example: The family-owned mill was bought by a corporate predator and closed within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家家族磨坊被一家企业掠食者买下，一年内即关闭。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the animal word for the firm that treats other firms as prey rather than partners.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了动物词汇，指把其他公司当猎物而非伙伴的企业。

senses.title: Microbial predator
senses.titleCN: 微生物捕食者：猎杀细菌的单细胞生物
senses.definition: a bacterium or protist that kills and consumes other microbes
senses.definitionCN: 指杀死并消耗其他微生物的细菌或原生生物
senses.example: The soil bacterium is a microbial predator that drills into other cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这种土壤细菌是微生物捕食者，能钻入其他细胞。
senses.why: Scale shrinks but the role survives: a predator still captures and consumes, even without a mouth.
senses.whyCN: 尺度缩小了，角色却保留：即使没有嘴，捕食者仍然捕获并消耗。

senses.title: Half of a predator-prey pair
senses.titleCN: 捕食对的一半：与猎物相互定义
senses.definition: the hunting side of a paired relationship whose two populations rise and fall together
senses.definitionCN: 指成对关系中的狩猎一方，两个种群数量随之共同涨落
senses.example: The predator and its prey oscillate on offset cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者与猎物在错开的周期上振荡。
senses.why: Neither side can be defined alone: a predator is whatever eats the prey, and the prey is whatever the predator eats.
senses.whyCN: 任何一方都无法单独定义：捕食者就是吃猎物的一方，猎物就是被捕食者吃的一方。

senses.title: Predator control
senses.titleCN: 捕食者控制：为保护目标物种而猎杀
senses.definition: in wildlife management, the deliberate reduction of predator numbers to protect livestock or endangered prey
senses.definitionCN: 野生动物管理中指为保护牲畜或濒危猎物而有意减少捕食者数量
senses.example: Predator control around the nesting grounds is debated every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天，巢区周围的捕食者控制都会引发争论。
senses.why: Management turns the predator into a variable to be adjusted, which is why the word appears in policy rather than only in biology.
senses.whyCN: 管理把捕食者变成可调节的变量，因此这个词不仅出现在生物学，也出现在政策里。

senses.title: Predator satiation
senses.titleCN: 捕食者饱和：以数量洪流换存活率
senses.definition: an evolutionary strategy in which prey reproduce in overwhelming numbers so that predators cannot eat them all
senses.definitionCN: 指猎物以压倒性数量同步繁殖、使捕食者吃不完的演化策略
senses.example: Bamboo masting relies on predator satiation to let some seeds survive.
senses.exampleCN: 竹子的集体结实依靠捕食者饱和，让部分种子得以存活。
senses.why: The term names the predator as a limiting filter: the strategy works only if the predator's appetite is finite.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把捕食者当作限制性过滤器：策略生效的前提是捕食者的胃口有限。

intro.en: Predator is an English agent noun on Latin praedator 'plunderer', from praeda 'booty'. It began as a word for a raider before ecology made it a word for a hunter.
intro.cn: predator 是英语在拉丁语 praedator「劫掠者」上构成的施动名词，praedator 又出自 praeda「战利品」。它最初指劫掠者，后来被生态学变成捕猎者。

items.en: Praeda meant booty or prey, and the same root produced prey in French and predation in English.
items.cn: praeda 意为战利品或猎物，同一词根在法语中产生 prey，在英语中产生 predation。

items.en: Praedator named a plunderer or raider. Its suffix -tor marks the person who performs the act.
items.cn: praedator 指劫掠者、抢夺者，后缀 -tor 标出执行该行为的人。

items.en: English predator appears in the nineteenth century, first in the raiding sense. The exact first citation is uncertain, and it is generally placed around the 1860s to 1870s.
items.cn: 英语 predator 在 19 世纪出现，最初取劫掠义；确切首见书证存疑，一般认为在 1860 至 1870 年代。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology made predator the standard word for a hunting animal, and the older human sense became figurative.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把 predator 定为狩猎动物的标准词，较早的人事义则退为比喻用法。

items.en: The word now covers corporate and criminal senses: a predator is anyone who treats others as expendable prey.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖企业与犯罪语境：凡把他人当作可消耗猎物的人，都可被称作 predator。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the actor, the act and the prey; the near-meaning group separates a behavioural role from a dietary class.
note.cn: 形近组区分施动者、行为与猎物；近义组区分行为角色与食性类别。

entries.definition: The process or event of killing and eating. A predator performs predation; predation is not the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死并取食的过程或事件。捕食者实施捕食；捕食不是动物本身。

entries.definition: Describes the hunting or exploitative quality. It modifies behaviour, prices or firms, not the animal as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述捕猎或掠夺的性质，修饰行为、价格或企业，而不是作为名词指动物。

entries.tag: an older synonym for the adjective
entries.definition: A variant adjective meaning hunting or predatory, usually of insects and other invertebrates. It is not the noun for the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词异体，意为捕食的，多用于昆虫及其他无脊椎动物。它不是指动物的名词。

entries.definition: An animal whose diet is mainly flesh. A carnivore need not hunt, since it may be a scavenger, and a predator need not be a mammal.
entries.definitionCN: 指以肉食为主的动物。食肉动物未必捕猎，因为它可能是食腐者；捕食者也未必是哺乳动物。

entries.definition: One that pursues game. It stresses the chase and is used of humans as well as animals, while predator stresses the ecological role.
entries.definitionCN: 指追逐猎物者，强调追捕过程，可用于人也可用于动物；predator 则强调生态角色。

entries.definition: An organism that feeds on a host without usually killing it. It exploits, but it does not hunt and consume in the predatory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指寄生于宿主、通常不杀死宿主的生物。它也剥削，但不进行捕食意义上的猎杀与吞食。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: praeda 'booty' plus -tor 'one who': the one who takes.
normal.cn: praeda「战利品」加 -tor「做某事的人」：取走东西的那一方。

normal.en: The family runs predation, predatory, predacious, prey and depredation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 predation、predatory、predacious、prey、depredation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: apex predator, natural predator, predator control, predator satiation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：顶级捕食者、天敌、捕食者控制、捕食者饱和。

normal.en: A predator hunts; a carnivore eats meat. A scavenger may be a carnivore but not a predator.
normal.cn: 捕食者狩猎；食肉动物吃肉。食腐者可以是食肉动物，却不是捕食者。

normal.en: In business the word becomes corporate predator: a buyer that treats firms as prey.
normal.cn: 在商业中这个词变成企业掠食者：把公司当猎物的买家。

abstract.en: Picture a lion low in the grass, eyes fixed on the herd at the water.
abstract.cn: 想象狮子压低身子伏在草里，眼睛盯住水边的兽群。

abstract.en: Picture a bacterium drilling into another cell and draining it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细菌钻进另一个细胞并把它吸干。

abstract.en: Picture a fund buying a struggling factory, selling its machines and closing its gates.
abstract.cn: 想象一家基金买下经营困难的工厂，卖掉机器，关上大门。

examples.en: The removal of the apex predator changed the whole riverbank.
examples.cn: 顶级捕食者的消失改变了整片河岸。

examples.en: The bacterium is a predator of other microbes in the soil.
examples.cn: 这种细菌是土壤中其他微生物的捕食者。

examples.en: Regulators accused the fund of acting as a corporate predator.
examples.cn: 监管者指责该基金扮演企业掠食者的角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: preda（猎物）+ tor（者）→ 取走猎物的一方 → predator 捕食者

root: 拉丁 praeda「战利品、猎物」→ praedator「劫掠者」→ 英语 predator；20 世纪起成为生态学中「捕食者」的标准词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one role: the stronger party that takes. The prey may be a mouse, a microbe, a rival firm or a vulnerable person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一角色：取走东西的强势一方。猎物可以是老鼠、微生物、对手企业或弱势个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lion in the grass watching the herd at the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：草丛中的狮子盯着水边的兽群。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL ROLE: capture and consumption define the predator at every scale.
branches.cn: 动物角色：捕获与消耗在一切尺度上界定捕食者。

branches.en: POSITION: the apex predator is defined by having no predator above it.
branches.cn: 位置：顶级捕食者由「上方没有捕食者」来界定。

branches.en: PAIRING AND MANAGEMENT: the predator is half of a cycle, a target of culling and a limit that prey can satiate.
branches.cn: 配对与管理：捕食者既是周期的一半，也是被猎杀的对象，还是猎物可以将其填饱的限制。

branches.en: CORPORATE METAPHOR: firms that treat others as prey inherit the old raider sense.
branches.cn: 企业隐喻：把他人当作猎物的公司，继承了古老的掠夺者含义。

branches.en: THE WORD ITSELF: Latin praedator was a plunderer before it was a hunter.
branches.cn: 词本身：拉丁语 praedator 先指劫掠者，后指猎手。

intro.en: Predator is a Latin agent noun, so its ending -tor tells you it names the one who performs the act.
intro.cn: predator 是拉丁施动名词，结尾 -tor 告诉你它指执行该行为的一方。

latinIntro.en: Praeda is the root, praedari the verb, and -tor the agent suffix that English keeps in predator and competitor.
latinIntro.cn: praeda 是词根，praedari 是动词，-tor 是施动后缀，英语在 predator 与 competitor 中保留了它。

items.example: The hawk is a daytime predator.
items.exampleCN: 鹰是白昼活动的捕食者。

items.meaning: the act of hunting and eating
items.example: Predation limits the rodent population.
items.exampleCN: 捕食限制了啮齿动物数量。

items.example: The firm used predatory pricing.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司采用了掠夺性定价。

items.example: Predacious beetles control aphids.
items.exampleCN: 捕食性甲虫能控制蚜虫。

items.structure: Old French preie, from Latin praeda
items.example: The prey froze when the shadow passed.
items.exampleCN: 影子掠过时，猎物僵住了。

items.example: The flock's depredation ruined the crop.
items.exampleCN: 鸟群的掠夺毁掉了庄稼。

items.example: The island was predator-free before the rats arrived.
items.exampleCN: 老鼠到来前，这座岛没有捕食者。

items.example: The model tracks predator-prey cycles.
items.exampleCN: 该模型追踪捕食者与猎物周期。

items.example: The report noted the fund's predatoriness.
items.exampleCN: 报告指出了该基金的掠夺性。

definition_zh: 覆盖；盖住；包括；掩护
definition_en: to put something over or on top; to include or deal with a range of things
core_image: 一块布或一个盖子压在上面的画面
scene: 要下雨了，妈妈快步走到阳台，把晾着的被子搬了进来。 Please cover the fish bowl before the cat arrives.
sceneCN: 这里 cover 是「盖住」（第 1 个义项：把东西放在上面遮住）；句意是猫来之前请把鱼缸盖上。

pos.zh: 覆盖；盖住
包括；涉及
掩护；报道
封面；盖子

senses.title: To put something over the top
senses.definition: to place something over or in front of another thing so it is hidden or protected
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在另一物的上面或前面，使其被遮住或受到保护
senses.example: Cover the leftovers before you put them in the fridge.
senses.exampleCN: 把剩菜盖好再放进冰箱。
senses.why: The core image is a lid or cloth pressed down over a thing, so any act of shielding from above is cover.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是盖子或布压在东西上方，所以一切自上而下的遮盖都可以叫 cover。

senses.title: To include a range of topics or areas
senses.definition: to deal with or contain many things within one range
senses.definitionCN: 在一个范围内处理或包含多种事物
senses.example: This chapter covers how plants make food.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章讲的是植物如何制造养分。
senses.why: A big cloth lies across the whole table; in the same way, one word or lesson may lie across many topics.
senses.whyCN: 一块大布铺满整张桌子；同样，一个词或一节课也能铺满许多话题。

senses.title: To protect or hide for someone
senses.definition: to protect a person or keep them from being seen or blamed
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人，或使其不被发现、不被责怪
senses.example: Our keeper moved quickly to cover the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员迅速移动去封堵球门。
senses.why: Sheltering under cover keeps a soldier safe, so helping someone by standing between them and danger is also covering.
senses.whyCN: 躲在掩体下能让士兵安全，所以站到别人与危险之间保护他们也是 covering。

senses.title: To report an event as a journalist
senses.definition: to follow and report news about an event
senses.definitionCN: 对某事件进行跟踪报道
senses.example: Two school reporters covered the sports meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 两名校园记者报道了运动会。
senses.why: News spreads over the whole surface of an event like a sheet laid over it, so journalists cover events.
senses.whyCN: 新闻像铺在事件上的一层布覆盖全局，所以记者们「覆盖」事件。

intro.en: Cover traces back to Latin words about catching and covering over.
intro.cn: cover 可追溯到拉丁语中与「捕获、覆罩」相关的词。

items.en: The Latin co-operire meant to cover completely, with co- (together) plus operire (to cover).
items.cn: 拉丁语 co-operire 意为完全盖住，由 co-（一起）加 operire（覆盖）构成。

items.en: A related word capere, to seize, is thought by some scholars to be mixed in; the exact link is debated.
items.cn: 一些学者认为相关词 capere（抓住）也掺入其中；具体联系尚有争议。

items.en: Old French formed covrir, meaning to cover or protect.
items.cn: 古法语形成 covrir，意为覆盖、保护。

items.en: English borrowed coveren in the thirteenth century, meaning to cover over.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 coveren，意为盖上。

items.en: The noun cover for book covers and lids appeared later, and the verb spread to news and ranges.
items.cn: 名词 cover 指书皮和盖子出现较晚，动词义扩展到新闻和范围。

note.en: These words share the cover root or name things that hide or lie on top.
note.cn: 这些词与 cover 同根，或指遮盖、覆在上面的东西。

entries.definition: how much an event is reported or a plan protects
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖范围；报道量

entries.definition: to find something hidden, un-cover it
entries.definitionCN: 发现

entries.definition: to get back to health or get something back
entries.definitionCN: 恢复；找回

entries.definition: a bed cover
entries.definitionCN: 床罩

entries.definition: hidden, not open
entries.definitionCN: 隐蔽的（同源）

entries.definition: to put out of sight
entries.definitionCN: 隐藏

entries.definition: a thick cover for a bed; as a verb, to lie all over
entries.definitionCN: 毯子；覆盖

entries.definition: to protect from harm
entries.definitionCN: 保护；遮挡

entries.definition: to fold paper or cloth around
entries.definitionCN: 包裹

entries.definition: to wrap completely; also a paper holder
entries.definitionCN: 包裹；信封

normalIntro.en: The cover family and daily covers make the word stick.
normalIntro.cn: cover 词族和身边的「盖」让这个词扎根。

normal.en: co- + operire: cover fully, so cover means put over.
normal.cn: co- 加 operire：完全盖上，所以 cover 意为盖上。

normal.en: dis-cover: take the cover away, so discover means find.
normal.cn: dis-cover：把盖子拿走，所以 discover 意为发现。

normal.en: re-cover: cover again, so recover means get back.
normal.cn: re-cover：再盖回来，所以 recover 意为恢复、找回。

definition_zh: 遵守；容忍；持续；居住；停留；承受
definition_en: to accept or obey a rule, to tolerate something, or to remain in a place or state
core_image: 一个人站在原地不动，时间从身边流过
scene: 她把那枚旧罗盘挂在墙上，说它陪自己走过每一段航程。 The memory of that summer abided with her for years.
sceneCN: 这里 abide 是「持续存在、留在心中」（第 3 个义项：某事物长期存续）；句意为那个夏天的记忆在她心中留存多年。

pos.zh: 遵守；持续；停留
容忍；承受

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转为形容词，义为「持久的；不变的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「遵守；居住」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「遵守者；居住者」

senses.title: To obey a rule
senses.definition: to accept and act according to a rule, law, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 接受并按照规则、法律或协议行事
senses.example: All members must abide by the club's rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都必须遵守俱乐部的规则。
senses.why: Old English abidan meant 'to remain'; to abide by a rule is to remain inside its boundary instead of leaving it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 abidan 意为「停留」；abide by a rule 就是留在规则的边界之内，不越出去。

senses.title: To tolerate something
senses.definition: to put up with a person or thing one dislikes
senses.definitionCN: 忍受自己不喜欢的人或事物
senses.example: She cannot abide people who talk during films.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法容忍看电影时说话的人。
senses.why: Tolerating something is staying in its presence without walking away, so 'remain' turns into 'endure'.
senses.whyCN: 容忍就是在它面前待着而不走开，于是「停留」变成了「忍受」。

senses.title: To continue to exist
senses.definition: of a feeling, memory, or condition, to last
senses.definitionCN: 指情感、记忆或状况长期存续
senses.example: The old custom still abides in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老习俗仍在村中延续。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to remain; what remains over time is what continues to exist.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「停留」；随时间留下来的东西，就是继续存在的东西。

senses.title: To dwell somewhere
senses.definition: to live or stay in a place, now mainly literary or archaic
senses.definitionCN: 住在某地，现多用于文学或古语
senses.example: He abode in a small cottage by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在海边的一间小屋。
senses.why: A person who remains in one place is, in the old sense, dwelling there; the past form abode became a noun for a home.
senses.whyCN: 留在某地的人，按古老含义就是住在那里；过去式 abode 后来变成了表示「住所」的名词。

senses.title: To wait for something
senses.definition: to wait for a time or event, especially in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 等待某个时刻或事件，尤见于较早的用法
senses.example: We must abide the right moment to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须等待合适的发言时机。
senses.why: To remain in place until something happens is to wait for it; the waiting sense survives in older and literary English.
senses.whyCN: 在原地留到某事发生，就是等待；这个「等待」义保留在较早和文学化的英语里。

senses.title: To endure consequences
senses.definition: to accept and suffer the results of an action
senses.definitionCN: 接受并承担某一行为的后果
senses.example: Those who break the law must abide the consequences.
senses.exampleCN: 违法者必须承受后果。
senses.why: Enduring a result is remaining under its weight without fleeing; the same 'stay' image becomes moral stamina.
senses.whyCN: 承受结果就是在它的重压下留下而不逃开；同一个「停留」意象变成了道德上的坚韧。

senses.title: To remain faithful
senses.definition: to stay loyal to a faith, promise, or person
senses.definitionCN: 对信仰、承诺或某人保持忠诚
senses.example: They abode in their faith through years of hardship.
senses.exampleCN: 多年困苦中，他们坚守着自己的信仰。
senses.why: Faith is a place one stays in; abiding is refusing to move out even when conditions are hard.
senses.whyCN: 信仰是一个人停留的地方；坚守就是即使艰难也不搬离。

senses.title: To linger in a place
senses.definition: to stay in a place for a time rather than leave immediately
senses.definitionCN: 在某地待上一段时间，而不是立刻离开
senses.example: The scent of pine abided in the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 松木的气味留在空房间里。
senses.why: The concrete 'remain in place' sense applies to scents and presences that outlast their source.
senses.whyCN: 具体的「留在原处」义，适用于那些比来源留存更久的味道与气息。

intro.en: Abide is a native Germanic word meaning 'to remain', and most of its senses are extensions of staying in place.
intro.cn: abide 是一个本土日耳曼词，意为「停留」，它的大多数义项都是「留在原处」的延伸。

items.en: The root *bheidh- is reconstructed with the sense 'to wait, trust'; the reconstruction is standard but the semantic path is uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *bheidh- 被重构为「等待、信任」之义；这一重构是通行的，但语义演变路径不确定。

items.en: The Germanic verb *bidan meant 'to wait, remain', and it also produced the modern verb bide.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词 *bidan 意为「等待、停留」，现代动词 bide 也由它而来。

items.en: Old English abidan combined a- 'on' with bidan 'to wait', giving 'to remain, wait for'.
items.cn: 古英语 abidan 由 a-（在……上）与 bidan（等待）组合，意为「停留、等待」。

items.en: The past form abode also became a noun meaning 'a dwelling, a home'.
items.cn: 过去式 abode 同时演变为名词，义为「住所、家」。

items.en: The 'remain' sense survives chiefly in literary use, while 'abide by' became the everyday legal and moral phrase.
items.cn: 「停留」义主要保留在文学用法里，而 abide by 成为日常的法律与道德短语。

items.en: The negative 'cannot abide' developed from 'cannot remain with' into 'cannot tolerate'.
items.cn: 否定的 cannot abide 从「无法与之共处」发展出「无法容忍」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers the adjective, noun, and related native verbs; the second gathers verbs of obeying, tolerating, and remaining.
note.cn: 第一组收形容词、名词与相关的本土动词；第二组收表示遵守、容忍与停留的动词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning lasting or enduring, as in an abiding interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持久的、不变的」，如 an abiding interest（持久的兴趣）。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遵守；居住」，指遵守或停留的行为。

entries.definition: To wait or remain, as in bide one's time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「等待、停留」，如 bide one's time（等待时机）。

entries.definition: To carry out the orders or rules of another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「服从、遵守」，执行他人的命令或规则。

entries.definition: To allow something one dislikes to continue without protest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容忍」，不加反对地允许不喜欢的事物继续。

entries.definition: To suffer something difficult patiently over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受」，长时间耐心地承受艰难。

entries.definition: To stay in the same place or state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「保持、停留」，留在同一地点或状态。

entries.definition: To live in a place, or to keep thinking about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住」，也指持续思考某事。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two everyday patterns 'abide by' and 'cannot abide', plus the family of forms; the abstract hooks picture staying in place.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用两个日常结构 abide by 与 cannot abide，加上词族形式；抽象记忆点想象留在原地。

normal.en: Abide by the rules is the common legal and moral pattern for obeying.
normal.cn: abide by the rules 是表示遵守的常见法律与道德结构。

normal.en: Cannot abide means cannot tolerate, as in 'I cannot abide that noise'.
normal.cn: cannot abide 意为无法容忍，如「我受不了那噪音」。

normal.en: Law-abiding citizens keep the law; the -ing form works inside a compound.
normal.cn: law-abiding citizens 指守法的公民；-ing 形式可用于复合词中。

normal.cn: 过去式 abode 同时也是表示「住所」的名词。

normal.cn: bide 与 abide 共享古老的日耳曼语「等待」动词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from 'remain in place': staying inside a rule, staying beside what one dislikes, staying over time, and staying in a home or a faith.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都从「留在原地」生长出来：留在规则之内、留在不喜欢的事物旁边、随时间留存，以及留在住所或信仰里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing still while time moves past
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身影站着不动，时间从旁流过

branches.en: Staying inside a boundary: rules, promises, and faith are kept.
branches.cn: 留在边界之内：规则、承诺与信仰得到遵守。

branches.en: Staying under pressure: what one dislikes or suffers is endured.
branches.cn: 留在压力之下：不喜欢或艰难的事物被忍受。

branches.en: Staying over time: customs, memories, and scents persist.
branches.cn: 随时间留下：习俗、记忆与气味持续存在。

branches.en: Staying in one place: the old dwelling sense, now mainly literary.
branches.cn: 留在某地：古老的居住义，现主要用于文学。

branches.en: Staying until an event comes: the old waiting sense.
branches.cn: 留到事件来临：古老的等待义。

intro.en: The word is a native Germanic formation, so the useful pieces are the prefix a-, the stem bid-, and the endings that build the family.

senses.title: The business of banks
senses.definition: the business of taking deposits, lending money, transferring payments and keeping accounts for customers
senses.definitionCN: 吸收存款、发放贷款、转移支付并为客户记账的业务
senses.example: Banking grew quickly once the city allowed branch offices.
senses.exampleCN: 城市允许开设分行之后，银行业迅速扩张。
senses.why: The action noun turns the work done at a bank into the name of the whole industry.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词把银行里做的事变成整个行业的名称。

senses.title: Retail banking
senses.definition: services offered to individuals and small businesses, such as current accounts, savings and personal loans
senses.definitionCN: 向个人与小企业提供的服务，如活期账户、储蓄与个人贷款
senses.example: Retail banking moved most of its branches online.
senses.exampleCN: 零售银行业务把大部分网点搬到了线上。
senses.why: One branch of the industry serves ordinary customers, and the word often appears with retail to mark that side.
senses.whyCN: 行业的一支服务普通客户，这个词常与「零售」连用标明这一面。

senses.title: Commercial banking
senses.definition: lending and deposit services for companies, as distinct from investment dealing
senses.definitionCN: 面向公司的贷款与存款服务，与投资交易相区别
senses.example: Commercial banking and investment banking were once kept apart by law.
senses.exampleCN: 商业银行业务与投资银行业务曾由法律分开。
senses.why: The industry has a deposit side and a deal side, and commercial banking names the deposit and lending side.
senses.whyCN: 这个行业有存款一侧与交易一侧，商业银行业务命名的是存款与放贷一侧。

senses.title: Investment banking
senses.definition: raising capital and advising on mergers and securities for large clients
senses.definitionCN: 为大客户筹资，并就并购与证券提供建议
senses.example: Investment banking earned more in fees than in interest.
senses.exampleCN: 投资银行业务赚取的费用多于利息。
senses.why: The industry split into a deposit side and a deal side, and the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 这个行业分成存款一侧与交易一侧，这个词两面都涵盖。

senses.title: Central banking
senses.definition: the public function of managing a currency, interest rates and the stability of the banking system
senses.definitionCN: 管理货币、利率与银行体系稳定的公共职能
senses.example: Central banking became the main tool of crisis response.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行事务成为危机应对的主要工具。
senses.why: Above private banks sits a public authority, and its work is named by the same word with central in front.
senses.whyCN: 私人银行之上还有公共当局，其工作由同一个词加「中央」来命名。

senses.title: The banking sector
senses.definition: the industry as a whole, including all the firms that take deposits and lend
senses.definitionCN: 整个行业，包括所有吸收存款并放贷的公司
senses.example: Banking employs more people in the city than shipping does.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座城市，银行业雇用的员工多于航运业。
senses.why: A collection of firms doing the same work becomes a sector, and the word names that sector.
senses.whyCN: 做同一件事的一批公司构成一个部门，这个词命名该部门。

senses.title: Banking services
senses.definition: the concrete services customers receive, from payments to safe custody
senses.definitionCN: 客户获得的具体服务，从支付到安全保管
senses.example: Mobile banking made payments possible without a branch.
senses.exampleCN: 手机银行让支付不必再去网点。
senses.why: The abstract industry shows up in daily services, so the word also labels what a customer uses.
senses.whyCN: 抽象行业体现在日常服务中，因此这个词也标示客户所使用的东西。

senses.title: Banking regulation
senses.definition: the rules and supervision applied to banks, used as a modifier before nouns
senses.definitionCN: 适用于银行的规则与监督，用作名词前的修饰语
senses.example: Banking rules tightened after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后银行监管规则收紧了。
senses.why: An industry name used before a noun becomes an adjective-like label, which is how banking regulation and banking law work.
senses.whyCN: 行业名称放在名词前就带上形容功能，银行监管、银行法就是这样构成的。

intro.en: Banking is the action noun of bank, whose money sense comes from Italian banca 'bench' and Medieval Latin bancus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是「银行」的动作名词，其金钱义来自意大利语 banca「长凳」与中世纪拉丁 bancus。年代均为约数。

items.en: The money sense of bank goes back to a Germanic word for a bench, the table at which a money changer worked.
items.cn: 银行的金钱义可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「长凳」的词，即钱币兑换商工作的桌子。

items.en: Italian banca named the bench and then the money changer's business, and it is the direct source of the financial sense.
items.cn: 意大利语 banca 先指长凳，后指钱币兑换商的生意，是金融义的直接来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin bancus recorded the same bench and business, and it supplied the form that English borrowed.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 bancus 记录了同样的长凳与生意，并提供英语借入的形式。

items.en: English bank first named the money business and later the institution itself.
items.cn: 英语先以这个词指金钱生意，后指机构本身。

items.en: The English action suffix -ing produced banking, naming the business and then the whole sector.
items.cn: 英语动作后缀产生这个词，先指生意，后指整个部门。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation): the exact date of the action noun is not recorded, and the river sense of bank is a separate homonym.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：动作名词的确切年代未被记录，而「河岸」义是另一个同形异源词。

note.en: Group one separates banking from the institution, the person and the adjective; group two holds kinds of finance and the places money is kept.
note.cn: 第一组把银行业务与机构、人物、形容词分开；第二组是融资金融的种类与保管金钱的处所。

entries.definition: Bank is the institution or the verb to deposit; banking is the business carried on by such institutions.
entries.definitionCN: bank 是机构或「存钱」动词；banking 是这些机构从事的业务。

entries.definition: A banker is a person who works in or owns a bank, not the industry.
entries.definitionCN: banker 是在银行工作或拥有银行的人，不是行业。

entries.definition: Bankable describes something a bank will accept or finance, not the business itself.
entries.definitionCN: bankable 描述银行愿意接受或提供资金的东西，不是业务本身。

entries.definition: Embankment belongs to the river-bank sense of bank and has nothing to do with money.
entries.definitionCN: embankment 属于「河岸」义，与金钱无关。

entries.definition: Finance is the broader field of money management, of which banking is one organised part.
entries.definitionCN: finance 是更宽的资金管理领域，banking 是其中有组织的一部分。

entries.definition: Credit is the capacity to borrow or the lending itself, a core activity within banking.
entries.definitionCN: credit 是借款能力或放贷本身，是银行业务中的核心活动。

entries.definition: Financial services covers banking plus insurance, investment and payments.
entries.definitionCN: financial services 涵盖银行以及保险、投资与支付。

entries.definition: A treasury is the office or account where funds are kept, a function banks also perform.
entries.definitionCN: treasury 是保管资金的部门或账户，银行也承担这一职能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real bench origin, the real suffixes and the real sector phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的长凳词源、真实的后缀与真实的部门说法。

normal.en: The money word began at a bench where coins were changed.
normal.cn: 金钱义始于兑换钱币的长凳。

normal.en: The action suffix turns the work into the name of a business and then of a sector.
normal.cn: 动作后缀把工作变成生意名称，再变成部门名称。

normal.en: Retail, commercial, investment and central mark the four main branches of the industry.
normal.cn: 零售、商业、投资与中央标出这个行业的四个主要分支。

normal.en: Banking regulation and banking law use the industry name as a modifier.
normal.cn: 银行监管与银行法把行业名当作修饰语。

normal.en: The river sense of bank is a different word and must not be mixed in.
normal.cn: 「河岸」义属于另一个词，不可混入。

abstract.en: Picture a row of counters where money moves from hand to hand all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一排柜台，钱整天在手中流转。

abstract.en: Picture a bench that grew walls, a roof and a vault without changing its purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长凳长出墙壁、屋顶与金库，用途却没变。

abstract.en: Picture a city where the tallest buildings are all full of accounts.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，最高的楼里全是账目。

examples.en: Banking provides the payment system on which the rest of the economy depends.
examples.cn: 银行业提供支付系统，其他经济部门都依赖它。

examples.en: Online banking reduced the number of branch visits.
examples.cn: 网上银行减少了到网点的次数。

examples.en: Central banking became the first line of defence in the crisis.
examples.cn: 中央银行事务成为危机中的第一道防线。

root: 由「银行」加动作名词后缀构成。「银行」的金钱义来自意大利语 banca「长凳」，经中世纪拉丁 bancus 进入英语，指钱币兑换商工作的桌子及其生意；「河岸」义为另一同形异源词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one business: the work at the counter becomes an industry, then splits into retail, commercial, investment and central branches, becomes a sector, appears as daily services and finally as a modifier for rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一门生意展开：柜台后的工作先成为行业，再分为零售、商业、投资与中央四支，成为部门，体现为日常服务，最后成为规则的修饰语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of counters where money moves from hand to hand all day.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排柜台，钱整天在手中流转。

branches.en: THE BUSINESS AND THE SECTOR: counter work becomes a trade, then a whole industry.
branches.cn: 业务与部门：柜台工作先成为行当，再成为整个行业。

branches.en: THE ORDINARY COUNTER: individuals and small firms are served at the retail side.
branches.cn: 普通柜台：个人与小企业由零售一侧服务。

branches.en: THE TWO DEALS: lending to companies and raising capital for large clients.
branches.cn: 两种交易：向公司放贷，以及为大客户筹资。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ROOF: a central authority manages the currency and the system.
branches.cn: 公共屋顶：中央当局管理货币与体系。

branches.en: THE SERVICE AND THE RULE: what a customer uses, and what regulators impose.
branches.cn: 服务与规则：客户使用的东西，以及监管者施加的要求。

intro.en: Banking belongs to the bench family of words; its money sense and its river sense are separate homonyms.
intro.cn: 这个词属于「长凳」词族；其金钱义与河岸义是两个独立的同形异源词。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin bancus supplies the money sense; the river sense comes from a different northern source.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁 bancus 提供金钱义；河岸义来自另一个北方来源。

definition_zh: 毒性；毒力；有毒的程度；有害性
definition_en: the quality or degree to which a substance, treatment or condition can harm a living organism
core_image: 一排培养皿里，水蚤在不同浓度的药液中依次停止游动
scene: 实验台上，一排培养皿里的水蚤在不同浓度药液下依次停止游动。 The lab measured the toxicity of the runoff at several dilutions.
sceneCN: 这里 toxicity 指「受试物质对生物造成伤害的程度」（第 2 个义项：以不同剂量测得的毒性强度）；句意为实验室在几个稀释倍数下测定了径流的毒性。图中可辨识物件：培养皿、水蚤、不同浓度药液、记录表。

pos.zh: 毒性；毒力（不可数为主，复数指多种或不同程度的毒性）

forms.label: 复数（多种或不同程度的毒性）

senses.title: The quality of being poisonous
senses.definition: the property by which a substance can harm or kill a living organism
senses.definitionCN: 某物质能够伤害或杀死生物的性质
senses.example: The lab measured the toxicity of the runoff at several dilutions.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在几个稀释倍数下测定了径流的毒性。
senses.why: Toxicity is toxic plus -ity, the suffix of a state, so it names the state of being poisonous rather than the poison itself.
senses.whyCN: toxicity 是 toxic 加 -ity（状态后缀），因此命名的是「有毒这一状态」，而不是毒物本身。

senses.title: A measured degree in toxicology
senses.titleCN: 毒理学中可测量的强度
senses.definition: the numerical relation between a dose and the response it produces, such as the dose that kills half a test population
senses.definitionCN: 剂量与其引起的反应之间的数值关系，如使半数受试生物死亡的剂量
senses.example: The pesticide's toxicity was expressed in milligrams per kilogram.
senses.exampleCN: 这种农药的毒性以每千克体重毫克数表示。
senses.why: Toxicology made the word quantitative: every poison has a dose, and the degree of harm is a curve rather than a yes or no.
senses.whyCN: 毒理学使这个词量化：任何毒物都有剂量，伤害程度是一条曲线，而不是「是或否」。

senses.title: Acute versus chronic toxicity
senses.definition: the classification of harm by whether it follows one large exposure or repeated small ones over time
senses.definitionCN: 按伤害来自一次大剂量接触还是长期反复小剂量接触所作的分类
senses.example: Chronic toxicity appeared only after months of exposure.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性毒性在接触数月之后才显现。
senses.why: Duration changes the harm entirely, so the word is routinely split into two named kinds.
senses.whyCN: 持续时间会彻底改变危害，因此这个词常被分成两个具名的类别。

senses.title: Harm caused by a medical treatment
senses.definition: the damaging side effect of a drug, radiation or procedure at therapeutic doses
senses.definitionCN: 药物、放射或操作在治疗剂量下产生的损害性副作用
senses.example: The regimen was reduced because of liver toxicity.
senses.exampleCN: 由于肝脏毒性，这套方案被减量。
senses.why: Medicine needed a word for harm that comes from the cure itself, not from the disease.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个词来指「治疗本身带来的伤害」，而非疾病带来的伤害。

senses.title: Ecological toxicity
senses.definition: the harm a substance does to fish, insects, plants or soil organisms in the environment
senses.definitionCN: 某物质对环境中的鱼、昆虫、植物或土壤生物造成的伤害
senses.example: Aquatic toxicity testing uses fish, daphnia and algae.
senses.exampleCN: 水生毒性试验使用鱼、水蚤与藻类。
senses.why: Ecology asks not only whether a substance harms people but whether it harms the organisms that hold a system together.
senses.whyCN: 生态学不只问某物质是否害人，还问它是否危害维持系统运转的生物。

senses.title: A regulatory hazard class
senses.definition: a formal category assigned to a chemical according to the harm it can cause
senses.definitionCN: 按可能造成的危害给化学品正式指定的类别
senses.example: The label warns of reproductive toxicity.
senses.exampleCN: 标签警示具有生殖毒性。
senses.why: Regulation turns the measured property into a class, so a substance can carry a toxicity label before any incident occurs.
senses.whyCN: 监管把测得的性质变成类别，因此某物质在事故发生之前就可以带上毒性标签。

senses.title: The potency of a toxin or venom
senses.definition: the strength of a poison produced by an organism, measured by how little is needed to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 生物所产毒物的强度，以造成伤害所需的最小量来衡量
senses.example: The venom's toxicity varied between populations.
senses.exampleCN: 不同种群之间，这种毒液的毒性并不相同。
senses.why: Here the word measures a biological product, where small differences decide whether a bite is merely painful or fatal.
senses.whyCN: 这里衡量的是生物产物，微小的差别决定一次咬伤是疼痛还是致命。

senses.title: Social toxicity in online or group settings
senses.titleCN: 网络与群体中的社会性有害氛围
senses.definition: the degree to which a community, forum or conversation is abusive, hostile or emotionally damaging
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群、论坛或对话充满辱骂、敌意或情感伤害的程度
senses.example: Moderators scored the thread's toxicity before deleting it.
senses.exampleCN: 版主在删除这条帖子前给它评了有害程度。
senses.why: Platforms needed a measurable word for the harm done by words, and toxicity supplied a scale.
senses.whyCN: 平台需要一个可衡量的词来指「言语造成的伤害」，toxicity 提供了尺度。

senses.title: Abstract: systemic harm in an institution
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：制度内部的系统性毒害
senses.definition: a transferred use for the cumulative damage that norms, incentives or habits do to trust and health
senses.definitionCN: 转指规范、激励或习惯对信任与健康造成的累积损害
senses.example: The audit described the toxicity of the promotion system.
senses.exampleCN: 审计报告描述了晋升制度的毒害性。
senses.why: The medical frame survives: repeated small exposures, not one incident, produce the illness.
senses.whyCN: 医学框架仍然保留：致病的是反复的小剂量接触，而非单一事件。

intro.en: Toxicity is toxic plus the Latin state suffix -ity. The root goes back through Latin to Greek arrow poison. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: toxicity 是 toxic 加拉丁状态后缀 -ity。词根经拉丁语可追到希腊的箭毒。年代均为约数。

items.en: Toxon meant 'bow'. Its origin is uncertain and it may be a borrowing from a non-Greek language, so any older form offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: toxon 意为「弓」。其来源不确定，可能是借自某种非希腊语，因此凡为它给出的更早形式都属假说。

items.en: Toxikon (pharmakon) meant 'arrow poison', literally the thing belonging to the bow; its adjective toxikos gave Latin toxicus.
items.cn: toxikon（pharmakon）意为「箭毒」，字面是「属于弓的东西」；其形容词 toxikos 给出拉丁 toxicus。

items.en: Latin toxicum meant 'poison', and medieval Latin used it for both venoms and drugs.
items.cn: 拉丁 toxicum 意为「毒」，中世纪拉丁用它兼指毒液与药物。

items.en: English toxic appears in the seventeenth century as a learned adjective meaning 'poisonous'.
items.cn: 英语 toxic 在十七世纪作为学术形容词出现，意为「有毒的」。

items.en: The noun toxicity and the discipline of toxicology grew with nineteenth-century chemistry and medicine, when poisons had to be measured rather than merely named.
items.cn: 名词 toxicity 与毒理学随着十九世纪的化学与医学成长，因为毒物需要被测量，而不只是被命名。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin of toxon, first date of the noun): the bow word may be a foreign borrowing whose source is unknown, and no single earliest citation is fixed for toxicity, so its first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（toxon 的来源、该名词的首见年代）：「弓」这个词可能是来源不明的外来借词，toxicity 也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same poison family that are easily confused with the abstract noun; group two holds measures and states that are often substituted for toxicity.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「毒」词族、容易与本抽象名词混淆的形式；第二组是常被用来替换 toxicity 的度量与状态词。

entries.definition: Poisonous; it describes the property, while toxicity names the property as a measurable thing.
entries.definitionCN: 有毒的；它描述性质，而 toxicity 把这一性质作为可测量之物命名。

entries.definition: A poison made by an organism; a toxin has toxicity, but the two words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 生物制造的毒物；毒素具有毒性，但这两个词回答的是不同问题。

entries.definition: A condition caused by poisoning; it is the illness, not the property that caused it.
entries.definitionCN: 由中毒引起的病况；它是疾病，而非造成疾病的性质。

entries.definition: The presence of toxins in the blood; a clinical finding rather than a measure of poisonousness.
entries.definitionCN: 毒素存在于血液中；它是临床发现，而非毒性的度量。

entries.definition: The degree of damage a pathogen causes in a host; it is a property of the organism, not of a chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 病原体对宿主造成损害的程度；它是生物的属性，而非化学物质的属性。

entries.definition: The strength of a drug or poison at a given amount; toxicity is the harm it does, potency is how little is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 一定量药物或毒物的强度；toxicity 是造成的伤害，potency 是需要多少才起效。

entries.definition: The capacity to cause death, often expressed as a proportion; toxicity also covers non-fatal harm.
entries.definitionCN: 致死的能力，常以比例表示；toxicity 还涵盖非致死的伤害。

entries.definition: A source of possible harm; toxicity is one property that makes something hazardous.
entries.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的来源；毒性是使某物成为危险源的一种性质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Toxicity is toxic plus -ity, the suffix of a state: the state of being poisonous.
normal.cn: toxicity 是 toxic 加 -ity（状态后缀）：有毒这一状态。

normal.en: The root is Greek toxon 'bow', the poison first used on arrows.
normal.cn: 词根是希腊 toxon「弓」，最早用在箭上的毒。

normal.en: The family runs toxic, toxin, toxicology, toxicological and toxicosis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 toxic、toxin、toxicology、toxicological 与 toxicosis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: acute toxicity, chronic toxicity, toxicity test, toxicity level.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：急性毒性、慢性毒性、毒性试验、毒性水平。

normal.en: The two collocations acute and chronic split the word by duration.
normal.cn: acute 与 chronic 两个搭配按持续时间把这个词一分为二。

abstract.en: Picture daphnia stopping one by one as the dilution gets stronger.
abstract.cn: 想象随着稀释变淡又变浓，水蚤一只只停止游动。

abstract.en: Picture a medicine that cures one organ and slowly harms another.
abstract.cn: 想象一种药治好一个器官，却慢慢伤害另一个。

abstract.en: Picture a comment section where every reply makes the next one harsher.
abstract.cn: 想象一个评论区，每条回复都让下一条更刻薄。

examples.en: Toxicity depends on dose, duration and the organism exposed.
examples.cn: 毒性取决于剂量、持续时间与受试生物。

examples.en: The label lists acute toxicity and long-term effects.
examples.cn: 标签列出急性毒性与长期效应。

examples.en: Online platforms now measure toxicity in comments.
examples.cn: 网络平台如今会测量评论的有害程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「toxic（有毒的）+ ity」——有毒的程度 → 毒性

root: toxic + -ity；toxic 经拉丁 toxicus / toxicum「毒」出自希腊 toxikon「箭毒」，再出自 toxon「弓」，toxon 的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one property and one scale: the poison exists, a dose is given, a response is measured, duration splits it, medicine and ecology apply it, law labels it, and finally words and institutions are scored on the same scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一种性质与一把尺子展开：毒物存在，给出剂量，测出反应，时间把它分开，医学与生态各自应用，法律给它贴标签，最后言语与制度也用同一把尺子打分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of daphnia stopping at different dilutions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排水蚤在不同稀释浓度下依次停下。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND NUMBER: the quality and its measured degree are the same thing before and after the instrument.
branches.cn: 性质与数字：这一性质与它的测量值，是仪器前后的同一件事。

branches.en: TIME: one large dose and many small ones produce different illnesses.
branches.cn: 时间：一次大剂量与多次小剂量造成不同的病症。

branches.en: BODY AND ECOSYSTEM: a patient and a pond are both test cases for the same property.
branches.cn: 身体与生态：病人与池塘都是同一性质的受试对象。

branches.en: LABEL AND POTENCY: regulation fixes a class, biology measures how little is needed.
branches.cn: 标签与毒力：监管固定类别，生物学衡量需要多少才起效。

branches.en: TRANSFER: abusive speech and bad incentives are scored as if they were poisons.
branches.cn: 转移：辱骂言语与坏激励被当作毒物来打分。

intro.en: Toxicity is a Greek-Latin root with a Latin state suffix, so it can be read as poison plus degree.
intro.cn: toxicity 是希腊—拉丁词根加拉丁状态后缀，可以读作「毒 + 程度」。

latinIntro.en: Latin toxicum gives toxic, toxin, toxicity, toxicology and intoxicate; the suffix -itas appears in English as -ity in toxicity, rarity and paucity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 toxicum 衍生 toxic、toxin、toxicity、toxicology 与 intoxicate；后缀 -itas 在英语中作 -ity，如 toxicity、rarity 与 paucity。

items.example: The bow gave the poison its name.
items.exampleCN: 弓把名字给了这种毒。

items.example: Toxikon was smeared on the arrowhead.
items.exampleCN: toxikon 被涂在箭头上。

items.example: The Latin adjective became English toxic.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词变成了英语 toxic。

items.example: The suffix turns an adjective into a measurable state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成可测量的状态。

items.example: The water was toxic to fish.
items.exampleCN: 这水对鱼有毒。

items.example: Toxicity rose with concentration.

items.example: Toxicosis followed the contaminated feed.
items.exampleCN: 受污染的饲料导致了中毒症。

items.example: The filter detoxifies the water.
