definition_zh: 投掷；抛；（板球等的）球场；音高；推销；（船的）颠簸；沥青（名词）
definition_en: to throw something, or the level of a sound, a playing field, a sales talk, or a black sticky substance
core_image: 手臂一扬把球掷出——同样的动作在球场、音高、推销和沥青上各掷一次
scene: 投手咬着嘴唇看了一眼本垒，手臂一扬把球掷了出去。 The pitcher gave the ball a fast pitch toward the plate.
sceneCN: 这里是「投掷」（第 1 个义项：一次投球的动作）；句意为投手把球快掷向本垒板。画面就是那记干脆的投球。

pos.zh: 投掷；抛；搭（帐篷）；定调；推销
投掷；球场；音高；推销词；沥青

derivatives.zh: pitch 加 -er 构成的施动名词，义为「投手；水罐」
由 pitcher 与 plant 合成，义为「猪笼草；瓶子草」
pitch 的动名词，义为「投掷；（船）纵向颠簸」

senses.title: To throw something
senses.definition: to throw something with force, or to aim it at a target
senses.definitionCN: 用力扔出某物，或朝目标掷去
senses.example: He pitched the crumpled letter into the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把揉皱的信扔进垃圾桶。
senses.why: The basic arm-throwing action is the seed; every later sense plants this throw somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的挥臂投掷是种子；后面的义项都把这记投掷种到别处。

senses.title: To fix a tent or camp
senses.definition: to set up a tent in a place
senses.definitionCN: 在某处支起帐篷
senses.example: We pitched our tent on the ridge before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 天黑前我们在山脊上搭好了帐篷。
senses.why: Stakes are driven and lines thrown across the ground, so pitching a camp repeats the throw in pegs and ropes.
senses.whyCN: 打桩、甩绳，扎营的每个动作都是一次投掷的重演。

senses.title: The level of a sound
senses.definition: how high or low a musical note or voice is
senses.definitionCN: 乐音或嗓音的高低程度
senses.example: Her voice dropped to a lower pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音降到更低的音高。
senses.why: A thrown object rises and falls in an arc; a voice thrown into the air lands at a certain height.
senses.whyCN: 掷出的物体划出弧线；抛向空中的嗓音也落在一个高度上。

senses.title: A playing field
senses.definition: a marked area of ground on which a sport is played, used especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 划好界线的运动场地，尤用于英式英语
senses.example: The fans poured onto the pitch after the final whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响后球迷涌进球场。
senses.why: The game is pitched onto this square of ground, the same directed throw applied to the playing area itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛被「掷」上这块场地，定向的投掷挪到了场地本身。

senses.title: A sales talk
senses.definition: a planned talk meant to persuade someone to buy or agree
senses.definitionCN: 为说服他人购买或同意而设计的说辞
senses.example: He gave his pitch in ten sentences and closed the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他用十句话讲完推销词，签下了合同。
senses.why: The seller throws his offer at the buyer like a ball aimed at the strike zone.
senses.whyCN: 卖方像投手瞄准好球区一样，把自己的提议掷向买方。

senses.title: The rise and fall of a ship
senses.definition: the movement of a ship or aircraft when the front rises and falls
senses.definitionCN: 船或飞机的头部起伏的运动
senses.example: The storm made the ferry pitch heavily.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让渡轮颠簸得厉害。
senses.why: The bow rises and falls like an object thrown in an arc, so the motion borrowed the throw's name.
senses.whyCN: 船头像被抛出的物体一样起落，这种运动便借了投掷的名字。

senses.title: A black sticky substance
senses.definition: a thick black sticky substance made from tar, used for waterproofing
senses.definitionCN: 由焦油制成的黑色黏稠物质，用于防水
senses.example: The hull was sealed with pitch before the voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 出海前船壳用沥青封了缝。
senses.why: Pitched wood was thrown in the fire to make waterproof tar; the substance kept the old past-participle name.
senses.whyCN: 把劈开的木头（pitched wood）扔进火里熬出防水焦油，这种物质便沿用了那个过去分词的名字。

intro.en: English pitch is two words sharing one spelling: a Germanic verb of throwing, and an English past participle turned noun for tar.
intro.cn: 英语的 pitch 是两个词共用一个拼法：一个日耳曼源的投掷动词，和一个由过去分词转成名词的焦油词。

items.en: The throwing verb goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for stabbing or fixing, related to picking.
items.cn: 投掷动词源自一个表示「刺、钉牢」的重构日耳曼词根，与 pick 同源。

items.en: Pitch appeared in Middle English as a verb for throwing and driving in stakes.
items.cn: 中古英语中 pitch 已作动词，指投掷和打桩。

items.en: The substance sense comes from Old English pic, the past participle of piccan, to pitch wood for tar.
items.cn: 物质义来自古英语 pic，即 piccan（劈木熬焦油）的过去分词。

items.en: Sport, sound, sales and ship motion each extended the throw image from the Middle Ages onward.
items.cn: 从中世纪起，体育、声音、推销与船的颠簸各自延伸了投掷意象。

items.en: Modern use keeps all strands alive, from football pitches to elevator pitches.
items.cn: 现代用法把各条线都留着，从足球场到电梯推销词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers pitch's family and look-alikes; the near-meaning group gathers throws, fields and sound levels.
note.cn: 形近组收 pitch 词族与形近词；近义组收投掷、场地与音高词。

entries.definition: The player who throws the ball, and the jug he is named after.
entries.definitionCN: 投手，也指投手一词所借用的水罐。

entries.definition: A small piece of material or ground; spelled one vowel away from pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 补丁；小块地；与 pitch 仅差一个元音字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: A thin rod or a device that turns power on and off; rhymes with pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 细枝或电源开关；与 pitch 押韵，词源无关。

entries.definition: The general word for sending something through the air by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手把东西抛向空中的通称。

entries.definition: A light, careless throw, often upward.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻随意的一抛，常向上。

entries.definition: The marked area for tennis or basketball, the American sibling of pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 网球场或篮球场，是 pitch 在美式英语中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: All senses hang on one arm-throw; remember the throw and the rest follow.
normalIntro.cn: 所有义项都挂在一次挥臂投掷上；记住这记投掷，其余随之而来。

normal.en: One throw, seven lands: the bin, the campsite, the voice, the field, the deal, the ship, the tar.
normal.cn: 一掷七落：垃圾桶、营地、嗓音、球场、生意、船身、焦油。

normal.en: Pitch black is as dark as the tar sense of the word.
normal.cn: pitch black 与该词的焦油义一样黑。

normal.en: The pitcher of water and the pitcher of baseball share one family tree.
normal.cn: 水罐和棒球投手同属一棵家谱树。

normal.en: A sales pitch throws the deal at you; catch it or duck.
normal.cn: 推销词把生意掷向你；接住，或者躲开。

normal.en: High pitch is a note thrown high into the air.
normal.cn: 高音是被高高抛进空中的音符。

abstract.en: An arm swings back, then whips forward — the whole word lives in that swing.
abstract.cn: 手臂后摆再猛然前挥——整个词都活在这一挥里。

abstract.en: A ship's bow lifting and dropping on grey waves, again and again.
abstract.cn: 船头在灰浪上一起一落，反复不止。

abstract.en: Black tar bubbling in a fire of split wood, sealing the seams of a hull.
abstract.cn: 劈开的木头在火里熬出冒泡的黑焦油，封住船壳的缝。

examples.en: Pitch the ball to me and I'll catch it.
examples.cn: 把球抛给我，我来接。

examples.en: The singer hit every note at exactly the right pitch.
examples.cn: 歌手把每个音都唱在准确的音高上。

examples.en: Her pitch for the new app won over the investors.
examples.cn: 她对新应用的推销打动了投资人。

sensesIntro.en: One throwing arm explains a battlefield of meanings: the ball, the tent, the note, the field, the deal, the ship and the tar.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条挥掷的手臂解释了一片意义战场：球、帐篷、音符、场地、生意、船身与焦油。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm throwing something with force toward a chosen spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条手臂用力把某物掷向选定的地点。

definition_zh: 收割；收获（作业）；采集（数据、细胞、雨水、木材等）
definition_en: the activity of gathering a crop, or of collecting data, cells, water or wild resources
core_image: 收割机在田里来回，粮仓口不断落下的谷粒堆成小山
scene: 收割机沿田边转圈，脱粒后的谷粒从管道落进拖车，司机盯着满仓指示灯。 Harvesting continues until the field is bare.
sceneCN: 这里指「收割这一持续进行的作业」（第 1 个义项）；句意为收割作业一直持续到田里收空。

pos.zh: 收割；收获（作业）；采集

derivatives.zh: harvest + -er（施动者或工具）→ 收割的人；收割机
harvest + -ed（过去分词）→ 已收割的
post-（之后）+ harvest → 收获后的
pre-（之前）+ harvest → 收获前的

senses.title: The work of cutting and gathering
senses.definition: the ongoing work of cutting, picking and gathering a ripe crop
senses.definitionCN: 把成熟作物割下、摘下并收拢的持续工作
senses.example: Harvesting begins when the grain is hard enough to snap.
senses.exampleCN: 谷粒硬到能掰断时，收割就开始了。
senses.why: The -ing form names the activity as it happens rather than the single decisive act.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式命名正在进行的活动，而非单个决定性动作。

senses.title: The period of the work
senses.definition: the span of days or weeks during which the crop is gathered
senses.definitionCN: 收作物所用的数日或数周时间
senses.example: Harvesting overlaps with the start of the school year.
senses.exampleCN: 收割期与开学时间重叠。
senses.why: A season is defined by the activity that fills it, so the -ing noun can name the period too.
senses.whyCN: 季节由填满它的活动定义，因此这个 -ing 名词也能指该时段。

senses.title: Mechanical harvesting
senses.definition: gathering crops with combines, binders or other machines
senses.definitionCN: 用联合收割机、割捆机或其他机器收集作物
senses.example: Mechanical harvesting leaves less stubble for grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 机械收割留下的茬口较少，不利于放牧。
senses.why: Once machines take over the work, the activity splits by means rather than by purpose.
senses.whyCN: 机器接手后，这项活动按手段而非目的分化。

senses.title: Hand harvesting
senses.definition: gathering crops by hand, often for delicate or selective work
senses.definitionCN: 用手收集作物，常用于精细或选择性作业
senses.example: Hand harvesting protects the fruit from bruising.
senses.exampleCN: 人工采收保护果实不被碰伤。
senses.why: The same activity is contrasted with machines because the hand can choose and spare what steel cannot.
senses.whyCN: 同一活动与机器对照，因为手能挑选并保护钢铁做不到的东西。

senses.title: Automated data collection
senses.definition: the systematic or automatic gathering of data from users, sensors or records
senses.definitionCN: 从用户、传感器或记录中系统性或自动地收集数据
senses.example: Data harvesting happens every time the page loads.
senses.exampleCN: 页面每次加载都会发生数据采集。
senses.why: The crop image survives in digital form: information is already growing somewhere and is taken in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 作物意象以数字形式存活：信息已在某处生长，被大批取走。

senses.title: Removing cells or organs
senses.definition: the removal of cells, tissue or organs from a body for treatment, donation or research
senses.definitionCN: 从身体取出细胞、组织或器官，用于治疗、捐献或研究
senses.example: Organ harvesting must follow strict consent rules.
senses.exampleCN: 器官摘取必须遵守严格的同意规则。
senses.why: The medical activity keeps the literal image of taking a living supply at its peak.
senses.whyCN: 医学活动保留「在最佳时取走活材料」的字面意象。

senses.title: Collecting rainwater
senses.definition: the capture and storage of rainwater from roofs or catchments for later use
senses.definitionCN: 从屋顶或集水区收集并储存雨水以备后用
senses.example: Rainwater harvesting supplies the garden through dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水收集在旱月里供给花园。
senses.why: What falls freely is treated as a crop to be caught rather than a resource to be pumped.
senses.whyCN: 自然落下之物被当作待收的作物，而非待抽取的资源。

senses.title: Taking timber or wild stock
senses.titleCN: 采伐木材或捕取野生资源
senses.definition: the gathering of timber, fish or wild plants from a managed or natural population
senses.definitionCN: 从经营或自然种群中采集木材、鱼类或野生植物
senses.example: Timber harvesting is limited to the winter months.
senses.exampleCN: 木材采伐仅限于冬季数月。
senses.why: The gathering image extends to any standing supply, whether planted or wild.
senses.whyCN: 采集意象扩展到任何现成储备，无论栽培还是野生。

intro.en: Harvesting is the verbal noun of harvest, formed with the native English suffix -ing. The base word goes back to Old English hærfest, autumn. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: harvesting 是 harvest 的动名词，由英语本族后缀 -ing 构成。其基础词可上溯到古英语 hærfest「秋天」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hærfest named autumn and the gathering that filled it, so the later activity noun had a season already built into it.
items.cn: hærfest 指秋天与填满秋天的收作物，因此后来的活动名词自带一个季节。

items.en: The suffix -ing turns a verb into the name of its ongoing activity, as in harvesting, planting and threshing.
items.cn: 后缀 -ing 把动词变成其持续活动的名称，如收割、种植与脱粒。

items.en: Middle English used harvesting for the work of the fields before the noun harvest narrowed to the crop and the season.
items.cn: 中古英语已用 harvesting 指田间的活，后来名词 harvest 才收窄到作物与季节。

items.en: Machine reaping in the nineteenth century made harvesting a distinct operation with its own schedules and equipment.
items.cn: 十九世纪的机械收割使 harvesting 成为有独立日程与设备的作业。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries extended the word to data, organs, rainwater and timber.
items.cn: 二十与二十一世纪把这个词扩展到数据、器官、雨水与木材。

items.en: Source uncertain (base-word origin): the pre-Germanic root of harvest is reconstructed only, and the first use of the -ing noun is dated approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（基础词词源）：harvest 在日耳曼语之前的词根只有重构形式，这个 -ing 名词的首见年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms and compounds that are easily mistaken for the activity; group two holds nouns for taking in what has grown.
note.cn: 第一组是易被误当成「这项活动」的词形与复合词；第二组是表示「把长成之物收进来」的名词。

entries.definition: The base noun names the crop, the season or one decisive act; harvesting stresses the work as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 基础名词指作物、季节或一次决定性动作；harvesting 强调作为过程的工作。

entries.definition: A person or machine that does the work; it is the agent, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 做这项工作的人或机器；它是施动者，不是活动。

entries.definition: A long-legged arachnid named for its reaper-like shape; it has nothing to do with farm labour.
entries.definitionCN: 因形似收割者而得名的长腿蛛形动物，与农活无关。

entries.definition: The celebration after the work is finished; it marks the end of harvesting, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 工作结束后的庆祝；它标记收割结束，而非过程本身。

entries.definition: The cutting of grain, the first stage of the work; harvesting also includes gathering and hauling.
entries.definitionCN: 割谷，是工作的第一阶段；harvesting 还包括收拢与运输。

entries.definition: The general act of bringing scattered things together; harvesting is crop-specific and seasonal.
entries.definitionCN: 把散落之物聚拢的一般行为；harvesting 特指作物且具季节性。

entries.definition: The organized taking of items or data; it is neutral in tone, while harvesting keeps the agricultural image.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织地取走物品或数据；语气中性，而 harvesting 保留农业意象。

entries.definition: The practice of taking crops from land, often repeatedly; it names the land use rather than the gathering operation.
entries.definitionCN: 从土地上获取作物的做法，常为反复进行；它命名土地利用，而非收集作业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: harvest plus -ing: the work seen while it is still going on.
normal.cn: harvest 加 -ing：正在持续进行时被看到的工作。

normal.en: The family runs harvest, harvesting, harvester, harvested, harvestable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 harvest、harvesting、harvester、harvested、harvestable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the means: mechanical harvesting, hand harvesting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按手段分工：机械收割、人工采收。

normal.en: The same -ing noun appears in data harvesting and rainwater harvesting.
normal.cn: 同一个 -ing 名词出现在数据采集与雨水收集中。

normal.en: The season phrase harvesting season shows that the activity can name a period.
normal.cn: 短语 harvesting season 表明这项活动也能指一段时间。

abstract.en: Picture a machine tracing the field in ever-smaller rectangles until nothing is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器在田里绕出越来越小的矩形，直到什么都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a roof quietly filling a tank all winter without anyone carrying a bucket.
abstract.cn: 想象整个冬天屋顶悄悄把水箱装满，没有人提桶。

abstract.en: Picture a webpage that takes a small sample of every visitor and stores it in a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网页从每位访客身上取一小份样本，存进罐子里。

examples.en: Harvesting at night keeps the fruit cooler.
examples.cn: 夜间采收能让果实保持更低的温度。

examples.en: The company's data harvesting practices are under review.
examples.cn: 这家公司的数据采集做法正在接受审查。

examples.en: Rainwater harvesting reduced the farm's water bill.
examples.cn: 雨水收集降低了农场的水费。

dict_mnemonic.text: harvest（收割）+ -ing（进行中的事）→ 正在进行的收割；从麦田扩展到数据、器官、雨水与木材。

root: harvest + -ing；harvest 出自古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼 harbitas，更早的印欧来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ongoing activity: a crop is taken in, and the same taking-in is applied to data, organs, rain and timber.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一项持续活动展开：先把作物收进来，再把同一种「收进来」用于数据、器官、雨水与木材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine or a pair of hands moves across a ripe field, and the field behind it is empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：机器或一双手扫过成熟的田，身后的田已经空了。

branches.en: THE OPERATION AND ITS CALENDAR: the work and the weeks it occupies.
branches.cn: 作业与其日历：这项工作以及它占据的几周。

branches.en: THE MEANS: steel or hands, each with its own advantage.
branches.cn: 手段：钢铁或双手，各有优势。

branches.en: THE DIGITAL CROP: browsing behaviour is taken in like grain.
branches.cn: 数字作物：浏览行为像谷物一样被收走。

branches.en: THE BODY: living tissue is removed at its peak.
branches.cn: 身体：活组织在最佳时被取出。

branches.en: THE STANDING SUPPLY: rain, timber and wild stock are gathered from what is already there.
branches.cn: 现成储备：雨水、木材与野生资源都从已有的东西中收集。

intro.en: Harvesting is a native Germanic base plus the English suffix -ing, so the word can be read as a process noun built from an old season word.
intro.cn: harvesting 是日耳曼本族基础词加英语后缀 -ing，因此可以读作由一个古老季节词构成的过程名词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for the base word, so the Latin side is left empty; the family is Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；其词族属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The base noun still names the crop.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词仍指作物。

items.example: The suffix also builds planting and threshing.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 planting 与 threshing。

items.example: Harvesting stopped when the rain came.
items.exampleCN: 下雨时收割停止了。

items.example: The harvester broke down at noon.
items.exampleCN: 收割机中午坏了。

items.example: The harvested rows were left to dry.
items.exampleCN: 收过的行被留在地里晾干。

items.example: The lower field is not yet harvestable.
items.exampleCN: 低处的田还不能收割。

items.example: Preharvest spraying is restricted.
items.exampleCN: 收获前的喷药受到限制。

items.example: Postharvest handling decides the final price.
items.exampleCN: 收获后的处理决定最终价格。

items.example: A harvestman sat on the gatepost.
items.exampleCN: 一只盲蛛停在门柱上。

definition_zh: 多语的；使用多种语言的；多种语言并存的
definition_en: using or involving several languages, or able to speak several languages
core_image: 一块立在中转站的分区指示牌，同一行信息用四五种文字并排写出，行人抬头寻找自己的那一行
scene: 中转站的走廊上立着一块分区指示牌，同一行信息用四五种文字并排写出。 A multilingual notice board greeted arrivals in every language spoken along the route.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用多种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及多种语言并用）；句意为一块多语告示牌用沿线路途所讲的每种语言迎接抵达者。可辨识物件：指示牌、多行文字、走廊、行人。

pos.zh: 多语的；使用多种语言的
使用多种语言的人（较少用）

senses.title: Using several languages
senses.definition: describing a person, group or thing that works in more than two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述在两种以上语言中运作的人、群体或事物
senses.example: The reception desk is multilingual and answers in four tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 前台是多语的，能用四种语言应答。
senses.why: the word joins a prefix for 'many' to the root for language, so it simply counts tongues.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「许多」的前缀与表「语言」的词根相连，因此它只是数语言的数目。

senses.title: A society with many languages
senses.definition: describing a community in which several languages are in daily use
senses.definitionCN: 描述若干语言在日常中同时使用的社群
senses.example: A multilingual city can hold five languages in one market.
senses.exampleCN: 一座多语城市可以在一个市场里容纳五种语言。
senses.why: a city that keeps several tongues in daily use is the plural of a bilingual town, so the same adjective covers it.
senses.whyCN: 一座日常使用几种语言的城市，是双语城镇的复数形态，同一形容词自然覆盖。

senses.title: A text or sign in several languages
senses.titleCN: 用多种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: written or printed in more than two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种以上语言书写或印刷
senses.example: The airport's multilingual signs were redesigned after the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，机场的多语标牌重新设计过。
senses.why: the count becomes visible when the same words are printed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 当同一段话并排印出时，那个数目就变得可见。

senses.title: Multilingual education
senses.definition: schooling that uses several languages as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以多种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Multilingual education let children begin in the language of home.
senses.exampleCN: 多语教育让孩子从家里的语言开始学。
senses.why: a school that teaches through several tongues makes the count a policy.
senses.whyCN: 用几种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成了政策。

senses.title: Multilingual software
senses.definition: describing a program or platform that handles several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述能处理多种语言的程序或平台
senses.example: The multilingual platform switched language with one click.
senses.exampleCN: 这个多语平台一键就能切换语言。
senses.why: software can hold several language packs, so the old adjective was extended to code.
senses.whyCN: 软件可以装几套语言包，这个旧形容词因此被扩展到代码。

senses.title: Multilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how a mind stores and switches among several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对心智如何储存并切换多种语言的研究
senses.example: Multilingual speakers activate both lexicons at once.
senses.exampleCN: 多语说话者会同时激活两套词库。
senses.why: researchers ask whether the languages compete or cooperate, and the adjective names the case.
senses.whyCN: 研究者追问这些语言是竞争还是协作，这个形容词就指这种情形。

senses.title: A multilingual workplace
senses.definition: describing an organization whose staff routinely work across languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述员工日常跨语言工作的组织
senses.example: The hospital runs a multilingual helpline for new arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院为新到者开设多语求助热线。
senses.why: staff who answer in several tongues turn the adjective into a job requirement.
senses.whyCN: 用几种语言应答的员工，把这个形容词变成一项岗位要求。

senses.title: Multilingual resources
senses.definition: describing dictionaries, corpora or services provided in several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以多种语言提供的词典、语料或服务
senses.example: The archive released multilingual finding aids.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆发布了多语检索工具。
senses.why: once records and tools multiply languages, the word describes the shelf rather than the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 当记录与工具成倍增加语言，这个词便描述书架而非说话者。

intro.en: Multilingual joins multi- 'many', from Latin multus, to Latin lingua 'tongue, language' and the adjective ending -al. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把表「许多」的前缀与拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」及形容词词尾相连；该前缀出自拉丁 multus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus meant 'much, many'. Its comparative and related forms also gave English multi- as a combining element.
items.cn: multus 意为「多的、许多的」，其比较级与相关形式也为英语提供了表「多」的组合成分。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: The ending -alis built relational adjectives in Latin, and English -al does the same work.
items.cn: 拉丁语用形容词词尾构成关系形容词，英语的对应词尾承担同样的功能。

items.en: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century, when travel, trade and empire made many-language contact ordinary.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词，当时旅行、贸易与帝国使多语接触成为常态。

items.en: The late twentieth century applied it to software, education policy and brain research.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，它被用于软件、教育政策与脑研究。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first printed use of the English adjective is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个英语形容词最早的印刷使用年代不明，其在拉丁语之前的词根亦未知。

note.en: Group one holds the numbering words for how many languages are used; group two holds terms about language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是按语言数量编号的词；第二组是关于语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using exactly two languages; multilingual means more than two and often leaves the count open.
entries.definitionCN: 指正好使用两种语言；多语则指多于两种，且常不限定具体数目。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole and often appears in research contrasts.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是相反的一极，常用于研究对照。

entries.definition: The state or practice of using many languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指多语并存的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A person who speaks many languages, or an adjective for such a person; it stresses personal skill.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说多种语言的人，或描述此人的形容词，强调个人能力。

entries.definition: Relating to several cultures; a society can be multicultural while sharing one language.
entries.definitionCN: 指涉及多种文化；一个社会可以共享一种语言而同时是多文化的。

entries.definition: A term favoured in European policy for a person's partial skills across several languages.
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲政策偏好的说法，指个人在多种语言上各自不完整的技能。

entries.definition: The rules a state adopts about which languages it will use; the adjective alone does not imply policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家对使用哪些语言所作的规定；单用形容词并不含政策义。

entries.definition: The act of turning text from one language into another; multilingual describes the result, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指把文本从一种语言转为另一种；多语描述结果，而非动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first element means many, the second means tongue, so the word counts languages.
normal.cn: 第一个成分意为「多」，第二个意为「舌头」，因此这个词是在数语言。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to institutions: multilingual society, education, staff.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到机构上：多语社会、多语教育、多语员工。

normal.en: It stands above bilingual in a simple ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它在简单的阶梯上高于「双语的」：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs multilingualism, multilingually, bilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「多语现象」「以多语方式」「双语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A station sign with several scripts is the clearest picture of the word.
normal.cn: 写着几种文字的车站标牌，是这个词最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a single corridor where every passenger hears a different welcome.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每位乘客都听到不同的欢迎语。

abstract.en: Picture five doors into one room, each opened by a different key.
abstract.cn: 想象通向同一房间的五道门，每道由不同的钥匙打开。

abstract.en: Picture a brain holding several maps of the same city.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑里装着同一座城市的几张地图。

examples.en: The region has been multilingual for centuries, not only since tourism.
examples.cn: 这个地区几百年来一直多语并存，并非只因旅游业才如此。

examples.en: Multilingual ballots are required wherever literacy is uneven.
examples.cn: 在识字程度不均的地方，须提供多语选票。

examples.en: A multilingual corpus makes it possible to compare idioms across languages.
examples.cn: 多语语料库使跨语言比较习语成为可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马提林圭尔」——马背上驮着许多种语言一路走，这就是多语的。

root: 表「许多」的前缀出自拉丁 multus「多的」，后接拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」与形容词词尾；十九世纪英语构成该形容词，指使用或涉及多种语言。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take one count and spread it across persons, cities, signs, schools, software, minds, workplaces and archives.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项拿同一个数目向外铺开：人、城市、标牌、学校、软件、心智、工作场所与档案馆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sign board whose every line appears in four or five scripts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块指示牌，每一行都用四五种文字并排写出。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND THE MIND: more than two languages, held and used by one person.
branches.cn: 数目与心智：多于两种语言，由一个人持有并使用。

branches.en: A PLACE: cities and regions can hold several languages at once.
branches.cn: 一个地方：城市与地区可以同时容纳几种语言。

branches.en: A SURFACE: signs and documents show the count where everyone can see it.
branches.cn: 一个表面：标牌与文书把这个数目摆到人人可见之处。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: schools teach in several tongues, and workplaces answer in several.
branches.cn: 机构：学校用几种语言教学，工作场所用几种语言应答。

branches.en: TOOLS AND RECORDS: software and archives multiply the languages they carry.
branches.cn: 工具与记录：软件与档案馆成倍扩大其承载的语言。

intro.en: The word is a prefix plus a Latin root plus an adjective ending, and each part also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、拉丁词根与形容词词尾构成，每一部分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the language root; English -al mirrors the Latin adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 提供表数量的前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供「语言」词根；英语词尾对应拉丁形容词词尾。

items.example: The prefix answers the question how many.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀回答「有多少」。

items.example: The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。

items.example: The office keeps multilingual records.
items.exampleCN: 这个办公室保存多语记录。

items.example: Multilingualism is normal in border towns.
items.exampleCN: 在边境城镇，多语并存是常态。

items.example: The guide was written multilingually.
items.exampleCN: 这本指南以多语写成。

items.example: Bilingual staff covered the night desk.
items.exampleCN: 双语员工值守夜班台。

items.example: Monolingual forms excluded half the residents.
items.exampleCN: 单语表格把一半居民排除在外。

definition_zh: 植物的；植物学的；植物提取的
definition_en: relating to plants as living things, to the science that studies them, or to substances obtained from them
core_image: 标本夹里一片压平的叶子，旁边贴着写有拉丁学名的小标签
scene: 植物学家在标本册里压好一株蕨类，在标签上写下它的拉丁学名。 The field team pressed a fern into the specimen folder and wrote its botanical name on the label.
sceneCN: 这里 botanical name 中的 botanical 是「植物学名的；与正式拉丁学名有关的」（第 5 个义项：与正式拉丁学名有关）；句意：野外考察队把一株蕨类压进植物标本夹，并在标签上写下它的植物学名。场景要点：标本夹、压平的蕨叶、拉丁学名标签、采集标签。

pos.zh: 植物的；植物学的；植物提取的
（botanicals）植物提取物；植物性成分

derivatives.zh: 植物学上；从植物学角度
植物的；植物学的（多用于机构名称）

senses.title: Relating to living plants
senses.definition: relating to plants as living organisms, especially their structure, growth, and kinds
senses.definitionCN: 与作为活体生物的植物有关，尤指其结构、生长与种类
senses.example: The botanical survey recorded 240 species along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这次植物调查在山脊沿线记录了 240 个物种。
senses.why: The family chain runs botany → botanic → botanical, but -al does not add the meaning 'plant'. Latin -alis means 'pertaining to', so it turns botanic 'of plants' into an adjective of relation; the plant meaning sits in the Greek-derived stem botan-.
senses.whyCN: 这个词族的关系链是 botany → botanic → botanical，但 -al 并不添加“植物”这个意义。拉丁 -alis 意为“与……有关”，它把 botanic“植物的”变成表关系的形容词；植物义始终在希腊来源的词干 botan- 里。

senses.title: Belonging to the science of botany
senses.definition: belonging to botany as a scientific discipline, including its methods, names, and classifications
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为学科的植物学，包括其方法、命名与分类
senses.example: Botanical nomenclature follows strict international rules.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学命名遵循严格的国际规则。
senses.why: Because botanic already meant 'pertaining to the science of plants', adding -al lets the adjective describe the discipline itself. The reference shifts from the organism to the organized body of knowledge about it.
senses.whyCN: 由于 botanic 本已表示“与植物研究有关的”，再加 -al 就让形容词可以描述这门学科本身。指称对象从植物体转向关于植物的系统知识。

senses.title: Made from or obtained from plants
senses.definition: made from or obtained from plants, especially in medicine, cosmetics, or agriculture
senses.definitionCN: 由植物制成或从植物中提取，尤用于医药、化妆品或农业
senses.example: The cream contains botanical extracts rather than synthetic oils.
senses.exampleCN: 这款乳霜含有植物提取物，而不是合成油脂。
senses.why: This is metonymy: the source stands for the product. The adjective still names plant origin, but the noun it modifies is now an extract or ingredient, so the plant has been reduced to material.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻：来源代替了产品。形容词仍命名植物来源，但它修饰的名词已变成提取物或成分，于是植物被压缩成了材料。

senses.title: Relating to a garden or collection
senses.definition: relating to a place or collection where plants are grown, labelled, and shown for study or display
senses.definitionCN: 与种植、标注并展示植物以供研究或观赏的场所或收藏有关
senses.example: The botanical garden keeps a glasshouse for tropical species.
senses.exampleCN: 这座植物园为热带物种保留了一间温室。
senses.why: A botanical garden is a living archive: plants are arranged and labelled like research material. The adjective marks the place as scientific rather than merely ornamental, so the garden becomes an instrument of botany.
senses.whyCN: 植物园是一座活的档案库：植物被排列、标注，像研究材料。这个形容词标记该场所是科学性的，而不只是观赏性的，于是园圃成了植物学的工具。

senses.title: Relating to the formal Latin name
senses.definition: relating to the formal Latin name or taxonomic placing of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 与植物的正式拉丁学名或分类位置有关
senses.example: The botanical name for the common oak is Quercus robur.
senses.exampleCN: 普通橡树的植物学名是 Quercus robur。
senses.why: Naming is the most precise layer of botany. A botanical name is not a local label but a fixed Latin address that places the plant in a genus and species, so the adjective signals taxonomic exactness.
senses.whyCN: 命名是植物学中最精确的一层。botanical name 不是地方俗称，而是把植物固定在属与种中的拉丁地址，因此这个形容词标记的是分类学上的精确性。

senses.title: Noun: plant-derived substances
senses.definition: in the plural, substances or ingredients obtained from plants, used in cosmetics, supplements, or pesticides
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指从植物取得的物质或成分，用于化妆品、补充剂或杀虫剂
senses.example: Regulators require proof that botanicals are free of contaminants.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构要求证明植物提取物不含污染物。
senses.why: This is a zero conversion: the phrase 'botanical ingredients' drops its head noun, and the adjective remains as the class name. The plural botanicals then names the category of such substances.
senses.whyCN: 这是零派生：短语 botanical ingredients 省略中心名词，形容词留下来充当类别名。复数 botanicals 于是指这一类物质。

senses.title: Relating to scientific plant drawing
senses.definition: relating to accurate drawings or prints that record a plant's form so that it can be identified
senses.definitionCN: 与准确记录植物形态、以便识别之用的绘图或版画有关
senses.example: The herbarium keeps a botanical illustration of every type specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 标本馆为每一份模式标本保存一幅植物学插图。
senses.why: An identification drawing must show veins, hairs, and flower parts rather than a pleasing view. Botanical therefore marks the image as a diagnostic record, extending the adjective from the plant to the way it is documented.
senses.whyCN: 用于识别的绘图必须画出叶脉、毛被与花部，而不是一幅好看的景。botanical 因此标记这幅图是诊断性记录，把形容词从植物本身延伸到记录植物的方式。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanical versus botanic
senses.definition: both mean 'of plants'; botanical is the default modern adjective, while botanic survives mainly in fixed institutional names
senses.definitionCN: 两者都表示“植物的”；botanical 是现代默认形容词，botanic 主要残留在固定的机构名称中
senses.example: The Royal Botanic Gardens use botanic in their title, though the work done there is botanical.
senses.exampleCN: 英国皇家植物园在名称里用 botanic，但那里做的工作是 botanical 的。
senses.why: -ic and -ical are twin adjective endings built on the same stem. English specialised them: botanic stayed in older names such as botanic garden, while botanical took over general and technical use.
senses.whyCN: -ic 与 -ical 是同一词干上的成对形容词后缀。英语把它们分工了：botanic 留在 botanic garden 等较老名称里，而 botanical 接管了一般与技术用法。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanical versus herbal
senses.definition: botanical describes plant origin neutrally; herbal implies the traditional use of whole plants as medicine
senses.definitionCN: botanical 中性描述植物来源；herbal 暗示把整株植物作传统药用的做法
senses.example: A herbal tea is brewed from leaves; a botanical blend may be any plant-derived mixture.
senses.exampleCN: herbal tea 是用叶子冲泡的；botanical blend 则可以是任何植物来源的混合物。
senses.why: Herbal carries the older craft of gathering and brewing herbs. Botanical is the laboratory-neutral term, which is why a cosmetics firm prefers it: it claims a plant source without claiming medical action.
senses.whyCN: herbal 带着采集、煎煮草药的旧手艺色彩。botanical 是实验室式的中性词，因此化妆品公司更爱用它：它只声称植物来源，不声称医疗功效。

intro.en: Botanical is a derived adjective, not a root word. The Greek-derived stem names plants and pasturage; botanic entered English first, and -al made botanical from it. The modern family chain is often given as botany → botanic → botanical, but that is a chain of meaning and word formation, not a single line of descent.
intro.cn: botanical 是派生形容词，不是词根词。希腊来源的词干先表示植物与牧草；botanic 先进入英语，-al 再由它构成 botanical。现代常把词族链记作 botany → botanic → botanical，但那是意义与构词的链条，不是一条单向血统。

items.en: Greek botanē meant 'plant, grass, pasture, fodder', and botanikos meant 'of herbs'. Etymonline notes that the Greek words seem to have more to do with pasturage than with plants; related forms include botamia 'pastures, meadows', boter 'herdsman', and boton 'grazing beast'. The deeper origin of the family is not established.
items.cn: 希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、草、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”。etymonline 指出这些希腊词更多与放牧有关，而非与植物学有关；相关形式有 botamia“牧场、草地”、boter“牧人”、boton“吃草的牲畜”。这个词族的更深来源尚未确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin botanicus 'of plants' carried the Greek adjective into learned Latin, and French botanique (17c.) passed it into English. Latin had no native name for plant science, so this borrowed stem did the work.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 botanicus“植物的”把这个希腊形容词带入学术拉丁语，法语 botanique（17 世纪）再把它传入英语。拉丁语没有本土的植物科学名称，于是由这个借来的词干承担。

items.en: English botanic is recorded from the 1650s, meaning 'pertaining to the science or study of plants'. It came from French botanique or directly from Medieval Latin botanicus, and it is the shorter of the two English adjectives.
items.cn: 英语 botanic 于 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，意为“与植物研究有关的”。它来自法语 botanique，或直接来自中世纪拉丁语 botanicus，是两个英语形容词中较短的一个。

items.en: Botanical is recorded from the same decade, formed as botanic + -al. Latin -alis (through French -al) means 'of, like, pertaining to', so -al adds relation, not plant meaning. Morphologically botanical is botanic + -al; it is not built directly from botany with -ical.
items.cn: botanical 在同一时期有记录，由 botanic + -al 构成。拉丁 -alis（经法语 -al）意为“属于、像、与……有关”，所以 -al 添加的是关系，不是植物义。形态上 botanical 是 botanic + -al，并不是由 botany 直接加 -ical。

items.en: Botany, the name of the discipline, is recorded from the 1690s, formed from botanic with -y on the model of astronomy. Botanist is recorded from the 1680s as botany + -ist. Etymonline's dates make the person word appear slightly earlier than the field noun; that apparent contradiction means the exact derivation order is uncertain.
items.cn: 表示学科的 botany 于 17 世纪 90 年代有记录，由 botanic 加 -y、仿 astronomy 构成。botanist 于 17 世纪 80 年代有记录，按 botany + -ist 解释。etymonline 的年代让人这个词略早于学科名词；这一表面矛盾说明确切的派生先后存疑。

items.en: Modern usage extends the adjective from living plants to extracts, gardens, Latin names, drawings, and products. The 'plant-derived' sense is a later narrowing whose exact first date is not recorded. Botanical is now the neutral default, while botanic survives chiefly in institution names.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个形容词从活体植物延伸到提取物、园圃、拉丁学名、绘图与产品。“植物提取的”义是后来收窄出来的，其确切最早年代未见记录。botanical 现为中性默认词，botanic 主要残留在机构名称中。

note.en: The first group shares the botan- stem with different endings; the second separates plant-related adjectives by domain and by what part of the plant they stress.
note.cn: 第一组共享 botan- 词干而后缀不同；第二组按领域以及所强调的植物部位来区分与植物相关的形容词。

entries.definition: The older adjective from the same stem, now mostly fixed in names such as botanic garden. It lacks the general 'plant-derived' use of botanical.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的较老形容词，现多固定在 botanic garden 等名称中。它没有 botanical 那种一般的“植物提取的”用法。

entries.definition: The science that studies plants. It is the field itself, while botanical is the adjective of relation built on botanic.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的科学。它是学科本身，而 botanical 是建立在 botanic 上的关系形容词。

entries.definition: A person who studies plants. It shares botan- with botanical but adds -ist, so it names a practitioner rather than a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的人。它与 botanical 共享 botan-，但加上 -ist，因此命名的是从业者，而不是性质。

entries.definition: In botanical terms; from the viewpoint of plant science. The -ly ending makes it modify a verb or a whole statement, not a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从植物学角度；以植物学的说法。后缀 -ly 使它修饰动词或整句，而不是名词。

entries.definition: Relating to herbs used as medicine or flavouring. It stresses traditional preparation, while botanical merely states a plant origin.
entries.definitionCN: 与作药用或调味用的草药有关。它强调传统制法，而 botanical 只陈述植物来源。

entries.definition: Relating to flowers, not to plants in general. A floral scent comes from blossoms; a botanical survey covers mosses and ferns too.
entries.definitionCN: 与花有关，而非笼统与植物有关。floral scent 来自花朵；植物调查则连苔藓和蕨类也包含。

entries.definition: Relating to the cultivation of gardens. It names the growing practice, while botanical names the scientific study of the plants themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 与园圃栽培有关。它命名的是种植实践，而 botanical 命名的是对植物本身的科学研究。

entries.definition: Relating to plants as opposed to animals or minerals. It is a technical contrast word and rarely appears where botanical would do.
entries.definitionCN: 与植物有关，以区别于动物或矿物。它是技术性的对比词，很少出现在本可用 botanical 的地方。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Greek 'plant, fodder' stem, the twin endings -ic and -ical, and the living collocations botanical name and botanical garden.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：希腊语“植物、牧草”词干、成对后缀 -ic 与 -ical，以及真实搭配 botanical name、botanical garden。

normal.en: botanic + -al = botanical. The -al only adds 'pertaining to'; the plant meaning comes from the Greek-derived stem.
normal.cn: botanic + -al = botanical。-al 只添加“与……有关”；植物义来自希腊来源的词干。

normal.en: Greek botanē was fodder and pasture before it was a science; the same word fed animals and later fed scholars.
normal.cn: 希腊语 botanē 先是牧草与牧场，后来才成为科学；同一个词先喂养牲畜，后来喂养学者。

normal.en: botanic and botanical are twins from one stem. Older institutions kept the short twin; everyday English took the long one.
normal.cn: botanic 与 botanical 是同一词干生出的双胞胎。较老的机构留下短的那个，日常英语取了长的那个。

normal.en: A botanical name is a Latin address: genus first, species second, and the plant can be found from that address anywhere.
normal.cn: botanical name 是一个拉丁地址：先属后种，凭这个地址在任何地方都能找到这株植物。

normal.en: Botanicals in a cream are the plant parts reduced to ingredients; the adjective has become the noun for the material itself.
normal.cn: 乳霜里的 botanicals 是被还原成成分的植物部分；形容词已经变成指材料本身的名词。

abstract.en: A pressed leaf with a label: the moment a living thing becomes an object of knowledge is the moment botanical begins.
abstract.cn: 一片压平的叶子加一张标签：活物变成知识对象的那一刻，就是 botanical 开始的地方。

abstract.en: A herbarium drawer is an archive where plants are filed like documents, and botanical is the stamp on the folder.
abstract.cn: 标本馆的抽屉是一座档案库，植物像文件一样被归档，botanical 就是文件夹上的那枚印章。

abstract.en: A garden bed and a laboratory bench use one word because both arrange plants so that someone can look closely and name what is there.
abstract.cn: 花圃与实验台共用一个词，因为两者都把植物安排妥当，好让人靠近观察并说出那是什么。

examples.en: The botanical garden holds one of the oldest collections of alpine plants.
examples.cn: 这座植物园收藏着最古老的高山植物标本之一。

examples.en: Botanical extracts are listed separately from synthetic fragrance oils.
examples.cn: 植物提取物与合成香精油分开列示。

examples.en: Students learn to write a botanical description of a single leaf.
examples.cn: 学生学着为一片叶子写出植物学描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: “博坦尼克”——博物学家在植物园里给每片叶子贴标签 → botanical 植物的、植物学的

root: botanic（植物的）+ -al（拉丁 -alis，“与……有关”）；botanic 来自法语 botanique 或中世纪拉丁语 botanicus，再上溯希腊语 botanikos“草本的”、botanē“植物、牧场、牧草”；更早的联系存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of botanical follow one movement: take a living plant, press and label it, then let that label travel to extracts, gardens, Latin names, drawings, and products.
sensesIntro.cn: botanical 的九个义项沿着一条动作链展开：把活体植物压平、贴标签，再让这张标签延伸到提取物、园圃、拉丁学名、绘图与产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant is pressed, labelled, and named, so a living thing becomes an object of knowledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：植物被压平、贴标签、命名，于是一个活物变成了知识对象。

branches.en: PLANT LIFE AND DISCIPLINE: the adjective points first at the organism, then at the organized science that studies it.
branches.cn: 植物生命与学科：形容词先指向植物体，再指向研究它的系统科学。

branches.en: MATERIAL: the plant is reduced to an extract, and the adjective becomes the plural noun for such substances.
branches.cn: 材料：植物被还原为提取物，形容词又变成指这类物质的复数名词。

branches.en: PLACE AND NAME: a labelled garden and a Latin binomial are the plant turned into an addressable record.
branches.cn: 场所与名称：标注过的园圃和拉丁双名，都是植物被变成可检索的记录。

branches.en: RECORD AND TWIN: scientific drawing is documentation, and botanic marks the older institutional twin of botanical.
branches.cn: 记录与孪生词：科学绘图是文档化，而 botanic 标记 botanical 较老的机构用孪生形式。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: herbal marks the traditional medicinal edge that botanical avoids by staying neutral.
branches.cn: 边界：herbal 标出传统药用的边缘，而 botanical 以中性立场避开它。

intro.en: Botanical has no live English prefix. It is botanic + -al; the Greek and Latin material sits frozen inside the stem, and English can still add -ly to the finished adjective.
intro.cn: botanical 没有活的英语前缀。它是 botanic + -al；希腊语与拉丁语材料凝固在词干内部，英语还能在成品形容词后加 -ly。

latinIntro.en: One Greek stem botan- runs through botany, botanic, botanical, and botanist. Greek botanē meant 'plant, pasture, fodder' and botanikos meant 'of herbs'; Medieval Latin botanicus carried both into the schools.
latinIntro.cn: 一个希腊词干 botan- 贯穿 botany、botanic、botanical 与 botanist。希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”；中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 把两者带入学术。

items.structure: botan- (plant stem) + -y (name of a field, on the model of astronomy)
items.meaning: the science of plants; the suffix names a domain of knowledge, not a person or quality
items.meaningCN: 植物学；后缀 -y 命名一个知识领域，而不是人或性质
items.example: Botany began as the description and naming of useful plants.
items.exampleCN: 植物学最初是对有用植物的描述与命名。

items.meaning: pertaining to the science or study of plants; the shorter adjective
items.meaningCN: 与植物研究有关的；较短的那个形容词
items.example: The botanic collection was catalogued by species.
items.exampleCN: 这批植物收藏按物种编目。

items.meaning: relating to plants or botany; the longer and now default adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；植物学的；较长且现为默认的形容词
items.example: The botanical survey listed every fern in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这次植物调查列出了山谷里的每一种蕨类。

items.meaning: a person who studies plants; the shift is from a field to its practitioner
items.meaningCN: 研究植物的人；语义从学科转到从业者
items.example: A botanist identified the moss as a new species.
items.exampleCN: 一位植物学家鉴定出这种苔藓是新物种。

items.meaning: in botanical terms; the adjective becomes an adverb of viewpoint
items.meaningCN: 从植物学角度；形容词变成表视角的副词
items.example: Botanically, the tomato is a fruit.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上说，番茄是一种果实。

items.structure: botan- + -ize (to act in a particular way)
items.meaning: to collect or study plants in the field; the suffix turns the field into an activity
items.meaningCN: 在野外采集或研究植物；后缀把学科变成活动
items.example: They botanized along the stream for the whole morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们整个上午沿溪采集植物。

items.meaning: plant-derived ingredients; the adjective has become a class noun
items.meaningCN: 植物提取物；形容词已变成类别名词
items.example: The label lists three botanicals and no synthetic perfume.
items.exampleCN: 标签列出三种植物成分，不含合成香精。

items.meaning: relating to how a particular people use plants
items.meaningCN: 与某一族群如何使用植物有关
items.example: Ethnobotanical fieldwork records which plants a village uses for medicine.
items.exampleCN: 民族植物学田野工作记录一个村庄用哪些植物作药。

items.meaningCN: 研究化石植物的古植物学
items.example: Paleobotany reconstructs ancient forests from fossil leaves.
items.exampleCN: 古植物学根据化石叶片重建远古森林。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to plants; the immediate source of botanic
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与植物有关的；botanic 的直接来源

latinEntries.meaning: of, like, pertaining to; the ancestor of English -al
latinEntries.meaningCN: 属于、像、与……有关的；英语 -al 的前身

definition_zh: 文盲状态；不识字；（某一领域的）基本无知
definition_en: the inability to read and write, or a lack of the basic knowledge needed in a particular field
core_image: 一张贴在诊所墙上的通知，字行密密麻麻，一个人站在前面反复打量却无法读出内容
scene: 诊所墙上贴着一张密密麻麻的通知，一位老人站在前面反复打量，最后转身问护士。 Illiteracy kept him from reading the dosage on the label himself.
sceneCN: 这里指「不识字的状态」（第 1 个义项：缺乏读写能力）；句意为他因不识字，无法自己读出标签上的用量说明。可辨识物件：通知、字行、老人、标签。

pos.zh: 文盲状态；不识字（通常不可数）

senses.title: Inability to read and write
senses.definition: the condition of being unable to read or write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 无法读懂或写出简短浅近文字的状态
senses.example: Illiteracy closed doors that a signature would have opened.
senses.exampleCN: 不识字关上了那些本可由一个签名打开的门。
senses.why: the noun is the negative twin of literacy, so its core is the plain absence of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是「读写能力」的否定孪生词，其核心就是字母的缺席。

senses.title: The measured rate in a population
senses.definition: the share of a population that cannot read, treated as a figure for reports
senses.definitionCN: 不能读写者在人口中的比例，被当作报告用的数字
senses.example: Illiteracy fell by a third in the decade after the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 扫盲运动之后的十年里，文盲比例下降了三分之一。
senses.why: governments needed a number to track, so the condition became a statistic under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要一个可追踪的数字，于是这种状态以同一名称变成统计量。

senses.title: Functional illiteracy
senses.titleCN: 能认字却读不懂日常文书
senses.definition: the state of having some schooling yet being unable to use print in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 虽上过学，却无法在日常生活中实际运用文字的状态
senses.example: Functional illiteracy hides behind a school certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 实用性文盲常常藏在毕业证后面。
senses.why: the word widened from absence of letters to inability to use them, which is harder to see.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「不认识字母」扩展到「不会使用文字」，后者更难察觉。

senses.title: Digital illiteracy
senses.definition: the lack of basic competence with computers and online services
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏使用计算机与网络服务的基本能力
senses.example: Digital illiteracy excludes people from services that moved online.
senses.exampleCN: 数字文盲使一些人被排除在已搬到线上的服务之外。
senses.why: screens introduced a new set of signs, and the old negative noun was reused for them.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕带来一套新的符号，这个旧的否定名词因此被用于其上。

senses.title: Scientific or numerical illiteracy
senses.definition: the lack of the basic ideas needed to judge scientific or quantitative claims
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏判断科学或数量主张所需的基本概念
senses.example: Scientific illiteracy makes a misleading chart hard to challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 科学盲使人难以质疑一张误导性的图表。
senses.why: a field's basic vocabulary is the alphabet one must know, so its absence takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 某领域的基本词汇就是必须认识的字母，其缺席因此沿用同一名称。

senses.title: Illiteracy as a policy problem
senses.titleCN: 作为公共政策议题的文盲现象
senses.definition: the condition viewed as a social problem that states try to measure and reduce
senses.definitionCN: 被国家试图测量并减少的社会问题
senses.example: The ministry treated illiteracy as an obstacle to economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 该部把文盲问题视为经济增长的障碍。
senses.why: once the condition is counted, it also becomes something to be governed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种状态被计数，它也就成了治理对象。

senses.title: Illiteracy in a region or group
senses.titleCN: 某地区或群体的文盲状况
senses.definition: the extent of the condition among a named population, such as rural women
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定人群（如农村妇女）中的普遍程度
senses.example: Illiteracy among older women remained the highest in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 年长女性的文盲程度仍是全国最高。
senses.why: once counted, the condition can be compared across groups, and the name travels with the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被计数，这种状态便可在群体间比较，名称也随之进入比较。

senses.title: Ignorance of a field's basic codes
senses.titleCN: 对某领域基本规则的无知（引申义）
senses.definition: a figurative lack of the basic vocabulary needed to take part in a field
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地缺乏参与某一领域所需的基本词汇
senses.example: Economic illiteracy made the debate impossible to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 经济盲使这场辩论根本无法跟上。
senses.why: the metaphor is complete once 'letters' means any system of signs a participant must read.
senses.whyCN: 当「字母」泛指参与者必须读懂的任一符号系统时，这个比喻就完整了。

intro.en: Illiteracy is the negative noun matching literacy, built on Latin illitteratus 'unlettered', itself in- 'not' plus litteratus 'lettered'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是与「读写能力」相配的否定名词，建于拉丁 illitteratus「不识字的」之上，后者由否定前缀加 litteratus「写有字母的」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural writings or a letter. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数指著作或书信。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus 'lettered, learned' was formed with an ending meaning 'provided with'.
items.cn: litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」由表「带有」的词尾构成。

items.en: The negating prefix in- assimilated to the following consonant, giving illitteratus 'unlettered, unlearned'.
items.cn: 否定前缀因后接辅音而同化，形成 illitteratus「不识字的、无学问的」。

items.en: English formed the noun in the seventeenth century, when schooling and printing made the lack of letters a visible social fact.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪构成这个名词，当时学校教育与印刷使「不识字」成为显见的社会事实。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word also named a rate to be counted, and from the late twentieth it was extended to digital and scientific fields.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词也指可计数的比率；二十世纪后期又扩展到数字与科学领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and the earliest printed use of the English noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个英语名词最早的印刷书证年代亦不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same root that differ only in endings; group two holds words naming a lack of knowledge.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、只差词尾的词形；第二组是表示知识缺乏的词。

entries.definition: Describes someone unable to read, or names such a person; the noun names the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不能读写的某人，或指这样的人；名词则指这种状态。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write; the two nouns differ only by a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指读写能力；两个名词只差一个前缀。

entries.definition: Means 'following the exact words' and has no negative force at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，完全没有否定含义。

entries.definition: Able to read and write; it is the exact opposite of the adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 指能读写，与形容词形式正好相反。

entries.definition: A general lack of knowledge; illiteracy is the specific lack of reading and writing.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指缺乏知识；文盲特指缺乏读写能力。

entries.definition: The lack of basic competence with numbers, coined as the counterpart of numeracy.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏数字基本能力，是仿「数字能力」造出的反面词。

entries.definition: An older literary word for uneducated; it is close but belongs to formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 较古雅的说法，指未受教育，意思接近但属正式书面语。

entries.definition: Having only fragmentary reading and writing; it sits between the two poles.
entries.definitionCN: 指读写能力零碎，处于两极之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is literacy wearing a prefix of denial, so the pair is learned together.
normal.cn: 这个词就是戴上否定前缀的「读写能力」，两个词宜成对记。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern fields: digital illiteracy, scientific illiteracy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代领域：数字文盲、科学盲。

normal.en: The condition is also a number, which is why the phrase illiteracy rate exists.
normal.cn: 这种状态也会变成数字，因此有「文盲率」这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs illiterate, literacy, literate, semiliterate.
normal.cn: 同族包括「不识字的」「读写能力」「识字的」「半文盲的」。

normal.en: Functional illiteracy is the hidden kind: a certificate without usable skills.
normal.cn: 实用性文盲是隐藏的一类：有证书，却没有可用技能。

abstract.en: Picture a notice whose lines turn into a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张通知，上面的字行变成一扇锁住的门。

abstract.en: Picture a map with no names, so every road looks the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有地名的地图，每条路看起来都一样。

abstract.en: Picture a key that exists but cannot be found when the door is closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙确实存在，却在门要关时找不到。

examples.en: Illiteracy among rural women fell sharply once village classes opened.
examples.cn: 乡村夜校开办后，农村女性的文盲状况迅速下降。

examples.en: Functional illiteracy can survive years of schooling.
examples.cn: 实用性文盲可以在多年学校教育之后依然存在。

examples.en: Scientific illiteracy leaves people unable to judge a risk for themselves.
examples.cn: 科学盲使人无法自行判断风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一里特乐西」——一个字母都认不得，里外都乐不起来，这就是文盲状态。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」加表「带有」的词尾成 litteratus「识字的」，再加否定前缀构成 illitteratus「不识字的」；英语十七世纪由此构成 illiteracy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an absence: letters, then usable print, then the tools of a screen age, then the codes of science and of whole fields, until the word finally names any basic ignorance a society decides to count.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一种缺席：先是字母，再是可用的文字，然后是屏幕时代的工具，接着是科学与各领域的规则，最后指社会决定加以计数的任何基本无知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dense notice on a wall that refuses to become words.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上密密麻麻的通知，始终不肯变成可读的词。

branches.en: THE BASE ABSENCE: not knowing letters is the oldest and plainest layer.
branches.cn: 基底缺席：不认识字母是最古老也最朴素的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED AND GOVERNED: once measured, the condition becomes a target for policy.
branches.cn: 被计数与被治理：一旦被测量，这种状态就成为政策目标。

branches.en: PRINT WITHOUT USE: schooling can leave people unable to handle real paperwork.
branches.cn: 有字却无用：学校教育可能仍留下不会处理实际文书的人。

branches.en: NEW CODES: screens and scientific claims each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新密码：屏幕与科学主张各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: WHO AND WHERE: the condition is unevenly spread, and it can be figurative as well.
branches.cn: 谁与何处：这种状态分布不均，也可作比喻用法。

intro.en: The word is the negative member of a small family built on a Latin root for a letter.
intro.cn: 这个词是建在拉丁语表「字母」词根上的一个小词族中的否定成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, literature and literal; litteratus gives literate, and with a negating prefix it gives illitteratus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 衍生出「字母」「文学」与「字面的」；litteratus 衍生出「识字的」，加否定前缀则成 illitteratus。

items.example: The prefix assimilates to the next sound, which is why it appears as il-.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀会与后一个音同化，写作同化后的形式。

items.example: The root names the smallest unit of print.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指印刷文字的最小单位。

items.example: The adjective describes a person furnished with letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述一个「带着字母」的人。

items.example: The negative form entered English through learned Latin.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式经学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: The label was once used for anyone outside formal schooling.
items.exampleCN: 这个标签曾用于任何未受正规教育的人。

items.example: Illiteracy was treated as a national problem.
items.exampleCN: 文盲被当作一项国家问题。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write
items.example: Literacy programs were funded by the province.
items.exampleCN: 识字项目由省里拨款。

items.example: Semiliterate readers need simpler forms.
items.exampleCN: 半文盲读者需要更简单的表格。

definition_zh: 犁；耕地；艰难推进；扫雪机；投入（资金）
definition_en: a farm tool that turns over soil; to turn soil; to move with force through something; a snowplow; to reinvest money
core_image: 犁铧切开草皮，翻出的土块整齐倒向一侧，后面跟着拉犁的牲口
scene: 铁犁切进草皮，土块顺着犁壁翻倒，草根朝上，后面跟着两头拉犁的牲口。 The plow turns the stubble under before the winter rains.
sceneCN: 这里指「翻土的犁具」（第 1 个义项：农具犁）；句意为犁在冬雨前把茬子翻到土下。

pos.zh: 犁；扫雪机
耕地；艰难推进；猛撞；投入（资金）

derivatives.zh: plow + -ing（动作名词）→ 耕地作业
plow + share（犁刀）→ 犁铧（语义偏移：指犁的切土部件）
plow + land（土地）→ 可耕地；犁地量（语义偏移：历史上作土地面积单位）
snow（雪）+ plow → 扫雪机；扫雪（语义偏移：把犁的动作用于清雪）

senses.title: The farm implement
senses.definition: a farm tool with a blade that cuts and turns over the soil before sowing
senses.definitionCN: 播种前切开并翻动土壤的带刃农具
senses.example: The plow was dragged to the field's edge.
senses.exampleCN: 犁被拖到田边。
senses.why: The implement is the core sense, and its shape, a blade plus a beam, drives every later extension.
senses.whyCN: 农具本身是核心义，其形状——刃加横梁——推动所有后来的扩展。

senses.title: To turn over the soil
senses.definition: to cut and turn the soil with a plough before planting
senses.definitionCN: 种植前用犁切开并翻动土壤
senses.example: They plow the lower field in November.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在十一月翻耕低处的田。
senses.why: The tool becomes a verb by the ordinary English route: use the object, and the object's name becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 工具按英语常见路径变成动词：使用该物，其名便成为动作。

senses.title: To move with effort through something
senses.definition: to advance slowly and forcefully through snow, traffic, a crowd or a long text
senses.definitionCN: 在雪、交通、人群或长文中缓慢而用力地前进
senses.example: She plowed through the report before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会前费力读完了报告。
senses.why: A plough pushes resistance aside in a straight line, and that feeling transfers to any difficult passage.
senses.whyCN: 犁把阻力推向一边并直线前进，这种感觉转移到任何艰难的通过。

senses.title: A snowplow, or to clear snow
senses.definition: a vehicle or blade for pushing snow off a road, or the act of clearing snow with one
senses.definitionCN: 把雪推离道路的车辆或铲板，或用其清雪的行为
senses.example: The snowplow opened the pass by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 扫雪机在中午前打通了山口。
senses.why: The machine does exactly what a plough does to soil, so the name moved from field to road.
senses.whyCN: 机器对雪做的事正是犁对土做的事，于是名字从田里移到路上。

senses.title: To crash into something
senses.definition: to collide violently with something, used in the phrase plow into
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈撞上某物，用于短语 plow into
senses.example: The truck plowed into the barrier.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车猛撞上护栏。
senses.why: The image is force meeting resistance without slowing, the same image as a blade entering soil.
senses.whyCN: 意象是力量遇到阻力却不减速，与刀刃进入土壤同一意象。

senses.title: To reinvest money
senses.definition: to put profits or savings back into a business or project
senses.definitionCN: 把利润或储蓄重新投入企业或项目
senses.example: They plowed the first year's profit into new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把第一年的利润投入新设备。
senses.why: Money is turned into the ground of a business the way a field is turned before a new crop.
senses.whyCN: 资金被翻进企业的基础，如同新一季作物之前翻田。

senses.title: The Plough asterism
senses.definition: the group of seven stars also called the Big Dipper, seen as a plough shape
senses.definitionCN: 又称北斗七星的七颗星，被看作犁的形状
senses.example: The Plough stood almost overhead at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜时北斗七星几乎在头顶。
senses.why: The seven stars trace a blade and a beam, so English and Irish sky lore named them after the tool.
senses.whyCN: 七颗星勾出刃与梁的形状，因此英语与爱尔兰的星空传说以农具命名它们。

senses.title: A historical land measure
senses.titleCN: 历史上的耕地面积单位
senses.definition: ploughland, a unit of land that one plough team could work in a year
senses.definitionCN: 犁地量：一队犁牛一年能耕完的土地单位
senses.example: The manor was assessed at five ploughlands.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园被估为五个犁地量。
senses.why: Land was measured by the work needed to till it, so the tool's name became an area unit.
senses.whyCN: 土地按耕作所需的工作量计量，因此工具之名成为面积单位。

intro.en: Plow goes back to Old English plōg, probably reinforced by Old Norse plógr, from Proto-Germanic plōgaz. The deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a Celtic word for a heavy plough is one hypothesis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: plow 可上溯到古英语 plōg，可能受古诺斯语 plógr 强化，来自原始日耳曼语 plōgaz。更早来源不确定；与凯尔特语表示重犁之词的关联是假说之一。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plōg named the soil-turning implement, and the word already carried the sense of the work as well as the tool.
items.cn: plōg 命名翻土农具，这个词已同时带有工具与劳作两种意思。

items.en: Old Norse plógr, used by Scandinavian settlers, probably reinforced the English form and its spelling.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚移民使用的古诺斯语 plógr 可能强化了英语形式及其拼写。

items.en: The Germanic form plōgaz is reconstructed from English and Norse evidence rather than recorded directly.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 plōgaz 是由英语与诺斯语证据重构的，而非直接记录。

items.en: The pre-Germanic origin is uncertain; a link to a Celtic term for a heavy plough has been suggested, and Latin plaustrum, a wagon, is sometimes mentioned, but neither is established.
items.cn: 日耳曼语之前的来源不确定；有人提出与凯尔特语表示重犁的词有关，也有人提到拉丁 plaustrum「车」，但两者都未获证实。

items.en: British English settled on plough while American English kept plow, so the same word has two standard spellings today.
items.cn: 英式英语定为 plough，美式英语保留 plow，因此今天同一个词有两种标准拼写。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no agreed pre-Germanic source exists, so any root offered for the word is a reconstruction or a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：没有公认的日耳曼语之前来源，凡为此词提出的词根均属重构或假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms and compounds built on plow that are easily mistaken for the tool; group two holds verbs and nouns for working the soil.
note.cn: 第一组是由 plow 构成、易被误当成农具本身的词形与复合词；第二组是表示翻土作业的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same word; it is not a different tool but a spelling variant.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写；它不是另一种农具，而是拼写变体。

entries.definition: The cutting blade of a plough; it is one part of the tool, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 犁的切土刀片；它是工具的一部分，不是整体。

entries.definition: A person who ploughs; it is the worker, not the implement.
entries.definitionCN: 犁地的人；它是劳动者，不是农具。

entries.definition: A vehicle or blade that pushes snow; it borrows the plough's action for a different material.
entries.definitionCN: 推雪的车辆或铲板；它把犁的动作借给另一种材料。

entries.definition: To prepare soil for crops; it is the general verb, while plow names the tool and the specific turning action.
entries.definitionCN: 为作物备土；它是普通动词，而 plow 命名工具与具体的翻土动作。

entries.definition: A narrow trench cut by a plough, or to make one; plow is the whole operation, furrow is its trace.
entries.definitionCN: 犁切出的窄沟，或挖出这样的沟；plow 是整个作业，furrow 是它的痕迹。

entries.definition: An implement that breaks clods and smooths soil after ploughing; it follows the plow rather than replacing it.
entries.definitionCN: 犁后打碎土块、平整地面的农具；它跟在犁后，而非替代犁。

entries.definition: To work land and grow crops over a season; plowing is one early step in that longer care.
entries.definitionCN: 在一季中耕作土地并种植作物；犁地是这段较长照料中的一个早期步骤。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: American plow and British plough are one word with two spellings.
normal.cn: 美式 plow 与英式 plough 是同一个词的两种拼写。

normal.en: The family runs plow, plowing, plowed, plowman, plowshare, plowland, snowplow.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 plow、plowing、plowed、plowman、plowshare、plowland、snowplow。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: plow a field, plow through, plow profits back.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：耕田、艰难穿过、把利润再投入。

normal.en: The snowplow does to snow what the plough does to soil.
normal.cn: 扫雪机对雪做的事，正是犁对土做的事。

normal.en: The Plough is a star shape, and ploughland is a land measure: tool, sky and area.
normal.cn: the Plough 是星形，ploughland 是土地计量：工具、天空与面积。

abstract.en: Picture a blade that turns darkness into a clean line of daylight.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀刃把黑暗翻成一条干净的光线。

abstract.en: Picture a reader pushing through a dense chapter as if it were frozen ground.
abstract.cn: 想象读者像推开冻土一样读过一个密集的章节。

abstract.en: Picture money being turned into the soil of a business, one furrow at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象钱被翻进企业的土壤，一沟一沟地翻。

examples.en: The farmer plowed the field before the first frost.
examples.cn: 农民在初霜前耕了田。

examples.en: The train plowed through the drifting snow.
examples.cn: 火车在堆积的雪中艰难前行。

examples.en: The company plowed its profits back into research.
examples.cn: 公司把利润重新投入研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: plow 是美式拼写，英式写作 plough；本义是翻土的犁，引申为「像犁一样推开阻力」——读书、撞车、清雪、把利润翻回企业。

root: 古英语 plōg「犁」，可能受古诺斯语 plógr 强化，源自原始日耳曼 plōgaz；更早来源不确定，与凯尔特语重犁词或拉丁 plaustrum 的关联均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blade: the tool, the turning of soil, pushing through resistance, clearing snow, crashing, reinvesting, a star shape and a land measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一把刀刃展开：工具、翻土、推开阻力、清雪、猛撞、再投入、星形与土地计量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade enters the ground and lays the soil over in a clean line, and the same push reappears in snow, traffic and money.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃进入地面，把土壤整齐翻到一侧，同一种推力又出现在雪、交通与金钱中。

branches.en: THE TOOL AND THE ACT: the implement and the soil-turning it performs.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：农具以及它执行的翻土。

branches.en: FORCE THROUGH: reading and crashing are two speeds of the same push.
branches.cn: 用力穿过：阅读与撞击是同一推力的两种速度。

branches.en: THE ROAD: snow is cleared by the same blade logic.
branches.cn: 道路：雪被同一套刀刃逻辑清除。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: profit is turned back into the ground of the business.
branches.cn: 账簿：利润被翻回企业的地基。

branches.en: SKY AND LAND: a star group and an area unit both take the tool's shape.
branches.cn: 天空与土地：一组星与一个面积单位都取了工具的形状。

intro.en: Plow is a native Germanic word with an uncertain deeper origin; its English family is built by spelling variation, suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: plow 是日耳曼本族词，更早来源不确定；其英语词族靠拼写变体、后缀与复合方式构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for plow; Latin plaustrum, a wagon, is sometimes compared but the link is a hypothesis, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: plow 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁 plaustrum「车」有时被拿来比较，但这一联系只是假说，因此拉丁部分留空。

definition_zh: 抽样；采样；抽样方法；抽样调查活动；音频与信号采样
definition_en: the process or method of taking samples from a larger whole
core_image: 一张方格地图铺在田埂上，每面小旗代表从一块田里随机取土的一个点
scene: 田埂上铺着一张方格地图，农技员按格子随机插上小旗，再从每面旗所在的位置取一撮土装进袋子。 Sampling began before sunrise, when the dew still lay on the leaves.
sceneCN: 这里指按一定方法从整体中抽取样本的过程（第 1 个义项：从较大整体中抽取样本的方法）；句意为抽样在天亮之前就开始了，叶子上还挂着露水。图中可辨识物件：方格地图、小旗、取土袋、记录板。

pos.zh: 抽样；采样；抽样方法；抽样活动

senses.title: The statistical method
senses.definition: the method of choosing a part of a population so that conclusions can be drawn about the whole
senses.definitionCN: 从总体中选出一部分、以便对整体下结论的方法
senses.example: Random sampling gives every member of the population a known chance.
senses.exampleCN: 随机抽样让总体中的每个成员都有已知的被抽中机会。
senses.why: Sample was a portion taken out, and the ending turns that action into a repeatable method.
senses.whyCN: 词根义为被取出的一份，后缀把这个动作变成可重复的方法。

senses.title: The act of taking one sample
senses.definition: one instance or occasion of taking a portion for testing or study
senses.definitionCN: 为检验或研究取出某一份的一次动作或场合
senses.example: Sampling took longer than the test itself.
senses.exampleCN: 取样花的时间比检验本身还长。
senses.why: The ending also names a single act, not only the method in general.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀也指单次动作，而不只是笼统的方法。

senses.title: The survey built on samples
senses.definition: a survey that studies a chosen part of a population instead of counting everyone
senses.definitionCN: 只研究总体中被选出一部分人、而非清点全部人的调查
senses.example: The survey relied on sampling rather than on a full count.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查依靠抽样，而不是全面清点。
senses.why: Once the method names an activity, the activity can be spoken of as a kind of survey.
senses.whyCN: 方法一旦命名一种活动，这种活动就可以被说成一种调查。

senses.title: Field collection of material
senses.definition: the collection of water, soil, air or plant material at a site for later analysis
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点采集水、土、空气或植物材料供日后分析
senses.example: Water sampling at the outflow is done twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 出水口的水质采样每周做两次。
senses.why: Environmental science uses the word for the physical gathering, because the portion must be carried away.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学用这个词指实物的采集，因为那一份必须被带走。

senses.title: Spot checks in production
senses.definition: the inspection of a few items from a batch to judge the whole batch
senses.definitionCN: 从一批产品里抽取少数几件检查，以判断整批
senses.example: Sampling of the finished bolts caught the faulty batch.
senses.exampleCN: 对成品螺栓的抽检抓出了那批次品。
senses.why: Factories apply the same logic as surveys, but the members of the batch are objects.
senses.whyCN: 工厂用的逻辑与调查相同，只是这批「成员」是物件。

senses.title: Audio sampling
senses.definition: the reuse of short recorded fragments in a new piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 在新音乐作品里重复使用短小录音片段
senses.example: The producer used sampling to rebuild the old chorus.
senses.exampleCN: 制作人用采样重建了那段旧合唱。
senses.why: A recorded fragment is a portion cut from a longer recording, so music kept the old word.
senses.whyCN: 录音片段是从较长录音里剪下的一份，音乐因此沿用旧词。

senses.title: Signal sampling
senses.definition: the regular measurement of a continuous signal at short intervals so that it can be stored digitally
senses.definitionCN: 按很短的时间间隔对连续信号反复测量，以便数字化存储
senses.example: Digital sampling turns a smooth wave into a series of numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 数字采样把平滑的波变成一串数字。
senses.why: Engineering takes portions of time instead of portions of material, and the word stretches to fit.
senses.whyCN: 工程取的是时间上的一份，而不是材料上的一份，词义随之伸展。

senses.title: The subject of a course
senses.definition: the branch of statistics that studies how samples are chosen and what they can prove
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中研究样本如何选取、能证明什么的分支
senses.example: The course begins with sampling and moves on to inference.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从抽样讲起，再进入推断。
senses.why: Any repeatable method can become a subject, and this one became a standard chapter of statistics.
senses.whyCN: 任何可重复的方法都能成为一门科目，而这一方法成了统计学的标准章节。

intro.en: Sampling is sample plus the English noun ending -ing. Sample itself is a clipped form of example, from Latin exemplum. The word's source is clear; only the date of its first record in each technical sense is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词由「样本」一词加名词化后缀构成，而该词本身是「例子」一词的缩略，来自拉丁 exemplum。词源清楚，只是各个技术义项最早记录的年代不确定。

items.en: Exemplum meant a sample or pattern, from eximere to take out; it is the remote source of sample.
items.cn: exemplum 指样本或范型，来自 eximere「取出」，是「样本」一词的远源。

items.en: The clipped English form sample is recorded in the Middle English period, with the first date uncertain.
items.cn: 缩略的英语形式在中古英语时期已有记录，首次年代不确定。

items.en: The Old English noun ending -ing turns a verb or noun into the name of an activity or its result.
items.cn: 古英语的名词化后缀把动词或名词变成活动或其结果的名称。

items.en: Statistical sampling took shape in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, when surveys began to rely on chosen parts rather than full counts.
items.cn: 统计抽样在十九至二十世纪成形，调查开始依靠选出的部分而不是全数清点。

items.en: Twentieth-century engineering and music gave sampling the senses of regular signal measurement and reused recorded fragments; the first dates of these uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 二十世纪的工程与音乐给了这个词定期测量信号与重复使用录音片段这两个义项；这些用法的起始年代不确定。

items.en: Modern survey work added fixed compounds such as sampling frame and sampling error.
items.cn: 现代调查工作又添上「抽样框」「抽样误差」这类固定复合词。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like sampling; the second names related steps in a study.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「本词」相近；第二组是研究里相邻的步骤。

entries.definition: The noun for the portion taken and the verb for taking it.
entries.definitionCN: 指取出的那一份，也指取这份的动作。

entries.definition: A device, person or collection that takes or holds samples.
entries.definitionCN: 取样器、取样者，或样品集。

entries.definition: The adjective for material that has been taken as a sample.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被取作样本的材料。

entries.definition: Identical; it only looks close and is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 相同的；只是形近，并无关联。

entries.definition: The list or map from which a sample is drawn.
entries.definitionCN: 抽取样本所依据的名单或范围。

entries.definition: The act of choosing the cases that will be studied.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选将被研究的案例的行为。

entries.definition: The gathering of material or data, often in the field.
entries.definitionCN: 在实地收集材料或数据。

entries.definition: A study that asks a chosen set of people for information.
entries.definitionCN: 向选出一批人索取信息的研究。

entries.definition: The act of assigning numbers to observations at intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 按间隔对观测赋予数值的行为。

entries.definition: The checking of a few items to judge a whole batch.
entries.definitionCN: 检查少数几件以判断整批。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real clipping, the real -ing ending and real technical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的缩略路径、真实的动名词后缀与真实技术复合词。

normal.en: Sampling is sample plus -ing: the activity built on taking portions.
normal.cn: sampling 是 sample 加 -ing：建立在「取出一份」之上的活动。

normal.en: Sample goes back to Latin exemplum and eximere, so every sampling keeps the picture of taking out.
normal.cn: sample 可追到拉丁 exemplum 与 eximere，因此每次抽样都保留「取出」的画面。

normal.en: Fixed phrases include random sampling, stratified sampling and sampling error.
normal.cn: 固定说法有随机抽样、分层抽样与抽样误差。

normal.en: Water sampling carries the portion away in a bottle; signal sampling carries away a slice of time.
normal.cn: 水质采样用瓶子带走一份实物；信号采样带走的是一段时间。

normal.en: A sampling frame is the list from which the choosing starts.
normal.cn: 抽样框就是开始挑选时所依据的名单。

abstract.en: Sampling is the art of letting a small part carry the weight of the whole.
abstract.cn: 抽样是让小部分承担整体重量的技艺。

abstract.en: Every method of choosing is also a method of leaving something out.
abstract.cn: 每一种挑选方法，同时也是一种舍弃方法。

abstract.en: The quality of the whole answer depends on how honestly the part was taken.
abstract.cn: 整个答案的质量，取决于那一份取得有多诚实。

examples.en: Sampling from the top layer alone would miss the heaviest grains.
examples.cn: 只从表层抽样会漏掉最重的谷粒。

examples.en: The team changed its sampling after the first results looked odd.
examples.cn: 第一批结果显得异常后，团队改换了抽样方式。

examples.en: Good sampling is invisible in the report and decisive in the conclusion.
examples.cn: 好的抽样在报告里看不见，却对结论起决定作用。
